section_ownership.note: Card D02-GEN-REST. Every top-level key of this file is labelled here, so no section is silently hand-maintained. `derived` sections are recomputed by the generator on every run and a hand edit to them is overwritten; `hand_maintained` sections are carried verbatim from the previous matrix, which is why a regeneration no longer reverts a later reconciliation; `integrator_supplied` numbers are measurements the generator cannot take.

header.purpose: A traceable requirement -> implemented profile -> source/model entry point -> executed test stage -> proof/evidence -> remaining-boundary matrix for revision 0.3 as implemented at this checkpoint.
header.counts_are_run_metadata: Every count in this file is run metadata about executed gates, manifests and archived measurements. A count is NOT proof of specification coverage: passing test totals, CT mapping counts, contract module counts and audit unit totals say what was executed, not what was proved. Projection coverage is not safety coverage and unknowns stay in the denominator.
header.verdict_vocabulary: Safe only after all obligations discharge; Unsafe only for a validated reachable violation; everything else Unknown. A provisional Unsafe is never presented as an upstream defect. Raw Cycle 19 units remain unpromoted.
header.independence_rule: The four evidence classes are marked INDEPENDENTLY per requirement. Support in one class is never inferred from another: a proved Lean theorem is not source evidence, an executed native run is not a model proof, and a model regression is not an observation.

evidence_classes.source: evidence taken on real source - QCore source programs through the frontend/driver, or C translation units through the gateway importers
evidence_classes.model: evidence taken in the dependency-free Rust kernel or the trusted verification adapter, over supplied traces, programs or certificates
evidence_classes.observation: evidence from an executed run - native/C11 execution, a CLI probe, a configured audit or a process provider
evidence_classes.mechanized: Lean 4 definitions and theorems registered in an Audit*.lean file and checked by scripts/check_lean_audits.py

support_status_vocabulary.executed: a named gate in the standing per-change gate runs this evidence class at HEAD
support_status_vocabulary.recorded_not_gated: the evidence exists as an archived probe log or transcript; nothing in the standing gate re-runs it
support_status_vocabulary.declared_premise: this class is an explicitly named assumption carried on the certificate/report, not established here
support_status_vocabulary.absent: no evidence of this class exists for this requirement
support_status_vocabulary.not_applicable: this class cannot apply to the requirement as stated

requirements.remaining_boundary: Observation scope/module/bounds substitution rejects; native provenance is declared trusted evidence and whole-program/source-model refinement remains open. Identity is provenance, not attestation: the compiler executable, its environment and the filesystem are trusted. Individual headers are not enumerated - the dependency closure is bound by effect through preprocessed_source_sha256 under -E -P, so a header edit that leaves the token stream unchanged does not change the identity. The declared driver is recorded, never checked for equivalence. The pinned Cycle19 compatibility adapter keeps CSourceInput::HistoricalStdin and its silent choice among 28 units with two or four compile configurations (G01 SS5); its four archived artifacts were not re-measured. Syntax and typed-AST phases still read preprocessed text from standard input, which is why __builtin_FILE/__builtin_FILE_NAME reject rather than being answered. P01-F2 is open: qcorec plugins verify/enable accept schema-valid, digest-intact edits to non-digest manifest declarations. P02 is not an OS sandbox: no namespace, cgroup, seccomp or capability-drop mechanism; no filesystem or network confinement (P03); RLIMIT_NPROC is per-UID and must not be presented as a per-execution child quota; non-Linux refuses rather than partially enforcing; the enforced profile is never selected by default.

named_followups.title: RLIMIT_NPROC conformance test is load-dependent
named_followups.why: a_declared_process_limit_stops_the_fixture_from_forking installs RLIMIT_NPROC=1, which counts every process of the real UID, so under load the host observes Io(Broken pipe) instead of Terminated. Two independent runs reproduced it; it passes in isolation and passed both merged full-gate runs. The assertion is deliberately not weakened. Wave-7 note: P03-F added a deterministic companion under the cgroup pids quota; the original assertion is byte-for-byte unchanged. Wave-17 note: GEN-CTREASONS measured a second load-sensitive row, `vp04_vp07_vp08_process_lifecycle_and_payload_budgets` (compiler/tests/cycle20_verifier_plugins.rs) — fails at load average 50, passes at load average 37 on the same binary — and EXTERN-MODES measured the confined-process fixture failing with Io(Broken pipe) under load and passing in isolation. Neither assertion is weakened; three rows are now recorded load-flakes to verify in isolation. Wave-26 note: two of the five recorded rows tripped across two cards' full-gate runs — the confined-fixture write test (EXAMPLES-SUITE-WIRE's first run) and the RLIMIT_NPROC row itself (its second, and CT-WIRE-LANE's) — each failing with character-for-character the same `Io(Broken pipe)` assertion, each verified in isolation at 12 passed / 0 failed on the same binary and the same tree, and each row passing on the run where its neighbour failed. No assertion was weakened and no test was re-run in isolation to obtain a pass. The same runs exposed a GATE defect rather than a test defect: `cargo test --workspace` is fail-fast, so one of these rows silently hid every target after it in crate order — a whole crate, `crates/qcorec/tests/examples_cli.rs` included — making the number that run printed a lower bound rather than a measurement. The integrator ADOPTED the fix at the wave-26 close: AGENTS.md's standing per-change gate now documents `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` (follow-on GATE-NO-FAIL-FAST), a deliberate STRENGTHENING, so a recorded flake can no longer shrink the suite it is reported against.

With nothing to migrate, `std.fmt`, `std.io` and `std.logger` are PROVIDED instead as `source.std-io.v1`: two renderings, a line to stdout, a level-tagged line to stderr and a `flush` barrier, each gated by its own module through the existing Q014/Q015 and refused without it, with Q028-Q031 under a new `StandardIo` pass through the §L21 process. The v1 effect discipline is STRUCTURAL rather than checked — the operand type has two constructors and neither can denote a resource, so a rendering cannot consume, release, store or retain custody, and the derived row is exactly {Io}, never Alloc, never Mut. named_followups.why: source.extern-call.unsafe.v1 landed in wave 18: an uncontracted external library links end to end behind import std.extern.unsafe; and unsafe extern fn, scalars by value in and a scalar or unit out, EVERY pointer refused by name (an assumption that cannot be stated cannot be carried, so no custody crosses), ExternAssumption::UncheckedLinkage carried on the existing declared-assumption channel with three independent omission guards and a Lean totality theorem, the Q023 default pinned unmoved, new pass UncheckedLinkage owning Q032-Q035. The prior workflow's NATIVE_LIBRARY_LINKAGE_V1.md is adopted into the tree (provenance-noted, band reservation moved twice, now Q039+) and reconciled with this card as one rule: pointers cross exactly where a contract exists to state their premise. Residual: UNSAFE-LINKAGE-ARTIFACT — the manifest-resident contract-less entry that would make the premise name WHICH artifact was waived, blocked on the library manifest itself not existing. UNSAFE-LINKAGE-ARTIFACT landed in wave 19 as level L1 of the linkage spectrum: a waived unsafe extern fn a manifest names publishes 'unchecked X at ABI S from artifact Y@hash under stated ABI premises' instead of the bare waiver, over a line-oriented total-or-reject manifest (fifteen named refusals, no catch-all) whose entries carry the C spellings so the agreement gate compares projections, not strings. The artifact identity is a PIN, not a probe — nothing is hashed at check time, because a premise must be rederivable from the program alone for Q027 recheck to reproduce it; a link-time substitution becomes a detectable premise violation rather than an invisible one. Band Q039-Q042 (NativeLibrary pass, the reserved band); qcore-schemas stays 14.0.0 (manifest types in qcore-core, constraint 18 not engaged). One recorded deviation: header disagreement REFUSES (Q041) rather than LOADER-ABI-withdrawing, because the only weaker reading here is the ACCEPTED bare waiver, so withdrawal would reward a contradiction with a premise that says less (pinned in Lean by a_named_symbol_is_never_admitted_bare). New: NATIVE-LIBRARY-CONTRACT-SLICE (where pointer symbols belong; prerequisite for L2/L3), NATIVE-LIBRARY-HEADER, NATIVE-LIBRARY-WITHDRAWAL, UNSAFE-LINKAGE-ARTIFACT-PROBE (builder-side hash observation, never a check), NATIVE-LIBRARY-SOURCE-BINDING, NATIVE-LIBRARY-MULTI-HASH; UNSAFE-LINKAGE-CLI narrowed (manifests selectable, contract environments still not). NATIVE-LIBRARY-CONTRACT-SLICE landed in wave 20: a manifest binds a symbol to a declared contract by MODULE REFERENCE (compared exactly, never normalised; total-or-reject in both directions), and a contracted call through it publishes ManifestResidentContract beside — never replacing — DeclaredContract, with a Q049 tripwire refusing a certificate that lost either half. Withdrawal direction argued as one rule with opposite polarities: withdraw only where the weaker admissible reading refuses (L1's weaker reading is the accepted bare waiver, so L1 refuses outright; here the weaker reading is the refusing uncontracted callee, so LOADER-ABI-style per-unit withdrawal applies, Q048). Band Q047-Q049 (a second NativeLibrary range; Q050 not taken — the waiver-mirror gate was written, measured unreachable behind Q034, and removed). Framing corrected: by the in-tree spectrum numbering this is L3's trust artifact; L3's source selection stays NATIVE-LIBRARY-SOURCE-BINDING. New: NATIVE-LIBRARY-SLICE-SHAPE, NATIVE-LIBRARY-CERT-REPLAY; NATIVE-LIBRARY-HEADER sharpened (the manifest now carries pointer spellings, so the header reader must reproduce the §C04 projection for them without a typed AST). Closed: NATIVE-LIBRARY-CONTRACT-SLICE, NATIVE-LIBRARY-WITHDRAWAL. NATIVE-LIBRARY-HEADER landed in wave 22: a manifest may name its exported header and digest (optional as a pair; byte-identical without), declarations read from the header's own token stream under a bounded directive subset, compared against the manifest's transcription; disagreement REFUSES (both sides are load inputs, and the weaker reading — a headerless manifest — is accepted); the header digest is VERIFIED (the decision is a function of the text) while the artifact hash stays a pin. Wave 23 landed L3's source selection and the decorated-header reader. NATIVE-LIBRARY-SOURCE-BINDING gives a source file its own binding: `extern library NAME;` at declaration position resolves that FILE against the one selected manifest declaring NAME, and everything else refuses — an unknown name, no manifest selected at all, two manifests declaring one name (ambiguous), a repeated binding, and a waived or contracted symbol of a manifest this file did NOT bind. An UNBOUND file is unchanged and still resolves selection-wide, which is what makes the card opt-in rather than a migration; a binding only ever NARROWS, and exactly where it removes a resolution the file is owed a refusal (Lean: a_binding_only_narrows beside a_narrowed_symbol_is_refused, which together are what keep this from being a weakening). Band Q065-Q067, NativeLibrary's FOURTH range, allocated through the §L21 process and contiguous with the third. The design document's SS2(a) recommendation and grounds are left UNEDITED - a decision record that rewrote its own reasoning after the fact would be worthless - and a new SS0 records the decision and what it changed about SS2(a): the prerequisite list it carried is the list for PARSING HTTP, not for constructing and checking it. named_followups.title: |> landed; || and && lowered onto branching in wave 19; singles reserved for bitwise
named_followups.why: Wave 18 landed the pipe operator |> as a pure token-stream desugaring (first-argument insertion, left-associative; byte-identical emitted C vs the hand-written twin; linearity through pipelines inherited from the existing checkers; a pre-existing divergent re-tokenization path in source_extern found and repaired). The measured surface bounds the rest: QCore has NO if statement (Q500; zero ifs across 294 source files) and no boolean expression tier, so the logical operators landed as claimed tokens with actionable refusals under the scope guards — single | is logical or and && is logical and BY DECISION, both refusing at Q038 until a lowering exists; || redirects to |, a lone & in logical position redirects to &&, bare & stays reserved for a future binary/bitwise operation, [| and |] are byte-unchanged, and bitwise OR having no symbol left is flagged open, not answered. The Pipe pass owns Q036-Q038 after an integration-time band relocation (UncheckedLinkage shipped Q032-Q035 first; the T07/T09 precedent). Residuals in dependency order: a source if/branching construct is the prerequisite for OR-LOWERING and AND-LOWERING; PIPE-CHAIN (multi-stage pipelines need expression-valued statements), PIPE-LET, PIPE-STMT-STAGES. Wave 19 landed the whole residual chain. IF-STATEMENT landed the branching prerequisite source.branch.v1 (if/else/else if, a decidable condition tier, custody-join agreement; band Q044-Q046; sequential route only with every other route's refusal pinned; ZERO new reserved words) and corrected wave 18's premise: five of six semantic models already branched internally — only cleanup_lowering lacked a branch constructor, so both arms flow through the existing checkers unedited and the conditional leak refuses through the pre-existing join net check. Then OR-AND-LOWERING SUPERSEDED the operator table by user direction: logical or is `||` (one token) and logical and `&&`, both short-circuit, admitted in the condition tier and lowered onto the branch construct with byte-identical emitted C against hand-lowered nested branches (associative on the nose for homogeneous chains, proved); single `|` and `&` refuse at Q038 with the bitwise reservation stated and `^` lexes as a reserved xor token — the open bitwise-OR-symbol note is RESOLVED (`|` is bitwise or, reserved). `&&` binds tighter than `||`, both left-associative, parentheses group; `|>` in a condition is refused, not ranked. No new code: Q045's tier widened and Q038's condition restated through §L21; Q043 went to ComposedStdIo. Five pins moved deliberately, no program's verdict changed; [| |] |> byte-unchanged. New: BITWISE-OPERATORS (needs an integer expression tier; inherits the longest-match constraint), IF-CONNECTIVE-NEGATION; from IF-STATEMENT: IF-RUNTIME-CONDITION, IF-ARM-ACQUIRE and -ATTRIBUTION (an acquiring arm refused by the pre-existing ownership join at Q103, measured and kept), IF-ARM-RETURN, IF-ARM-CALL, IF-ROUTE-WIDENING, IF-CONDITION-BINDINGS, SEQ-STATEMENT-TOKENS (the sequential driver still re-lexes source bytes; inert for conditions, recorded not repaired). named_followups.title: The first source-level aggregate type landed; fourteen residuals, each naming its missing capability
named_followups.why: AGGREGATES-V1 is wave 27's language head. source.record.v1 lands `type NAME { FIELD: i32, ... }`, `let p = NAME { FIELD: OPERAND, ... };` and `let a = p.FIELD;` on source.buffer.v1, with every OTHER route's refusal measured and pinned rather than widened, and route selection changing in exactly one condition - a record type DECLARATION - which no program written before the card can satisfy, because `type NAME {` did not parse at all. THE CARD'S DESIGN DECISION IS FIELD CUSTODY AND IT WAS MEASURED, NOT ARGUED: a v1 record is a plain copyable value whose fields are all i32, so it contributes NO qcore_core::ownership operation, opens no obligation and derives no effect - because the cycle-3 ownership IR addresses an owner by a plain NAME and has no notion of a path, so `p.buf` is not a question check_ownership can be asked. The consequences are the EXISTING route's rules rather than new ones: `drop p;` refuses at Q052 with 'is not a buffer this entry acquired', and a leak beside a record still refuses at Q054 with the inherited checker's own message. ZERO reserved words, and the constraint-14 census is why: the obvious spelling `record` was REJECTED ON EVIDENCE, because docs/reports/remaining-v07/probes/d02_boundary_record.qcore is the single line `record R { }` and TWO ARCHIVED REPORTS PIN IT TO Q000, so claiming the word would have falsified a frozen archive (constraint 21) - the syntax was renamed rather than the pinned surface edited, character for character the buffer -> bytes and work -> effort shape. `struct` is census-clean and was still not taken, on the ground that the language already has a declaration head for a named type. ZERO new diagnostic codes: Q051, Q052 and Q053's conditions are widened and stated in SS L21 under the Q-NAMESPACE-DECISION ice box, which the wave's language head therefore respected rather than being excused from. NO LINE OF NAME RESOLUTION CHANGED EITHER, and that too was a measurement: a field name sits before a `:` at a construction and after a `.` at a read, and frontend::lexical_references has drained both positions since long before the card, so a construction of an undeclared type refuses at Q013 as an ordinary unknown reference. The `.` adjacency is PINNED rather than assumed - `p.x` is Word Dot Word and cannot collapse into a float, so SOCKET-INET-ADDRESSES' Float Dot Float reading of 127.0.0.1 is untouched, and a NUMERIC field path is one float token and refuses by name. The census also ran in the other direction and found the six whole-token-stream route-selector words, whose collision is fail-closed in both halves (Q015 declared, Q000 constructed) - NATIVE-LIBRARY-SOURCE-BINDING's span exclusion was measured and DELIBERATELY NOT COPIED, because it would retire the Q015 half and leave a type that declares and cannot be constructed. Records emit real C structs with one distinctly named member per field behind load-bearing prefixes, and the payoff is CT09's own scenario EXECUTED - three declared fields, three different values, three reads, byte-compared against a sanitized ASan/UBSan/LSan run, so a lowering that gave two fields one member would print one value twice. One emission change lands outside the aggregate and is byte-neutral by an argument about which programs the emitter can reach (a buffer-free program now carries no buffer prelude, forced by -Wall -Wextra -Werror on an unused static); byte identity is MEASURED rather than asserted, the base commit's compiler rebuilt in a scratch tree and all 80 emitting programs compared byte-identical. 56 tests, 28 audited Lean entries in one new audit file, no new axiom. Corpus-neutral by construction. Standing constraint 15k records the decision. New, each naming its missing capability: AGGREGATE-OWNED-FIELD (a field that owns a resource - needs a field-path owner vocabulary, a partial-move rule, a drop-through-aggregate rule and a leak rule at normal exit that sees into the aggregate, none of which exists), AGGREGATE-VIEW-FIELD (a string field - smaller, but needs source.string.v1's exact borrow window, constraint 15h, to reach through an aggregate), AGGREGATE-FIELD-WRITE (`p.x = 5;` - cheap on this model but adds a rule to every composition), AGGREGATE-FIELD-TYPES (a field of a type other than i32), AGGREGATE-NESTED (a record field whose type is another record - needs a recursive rule and a termination argument for the declaration graph), AGGREGATE-ACROSS-CALL (a record-valued parameter or result), AGGREGATE-ROUTE-WIDENING (admitting the construct on the string, event, socket, HTTP, extern, task, mutex or epoch routes - each a separate checked model), AGGREGATE-STRING-COMPOSE (the composed string/buffer route, which refuses a record at Q068 today), AGGREGATE-BOUND-FROM-FIELD (a `for` bound read out of a field - known to the checker, not to the lowering, exactly LOOP-BOUND-FROM-BYTE's shape), AGGREGATE-REFUSAL-CASCADE (a refused construction leaves its binding unbound, so a later field read earns a second diagnostic; needs a poisoned-binding notion this route does not have, and the cascade is left alone rather than suppressed), AGGREGATE-LIBRARY-MODULE (a `module library;` file declaring a record, refused at Q058 today - a record type that outlives its file is a module-system question this revision's one-entry routes do not pose), AGGREGATE-SELECTOR-WORDS (the six route-selector words above), AGGREGATE-CT09-LAYOUT (CT09's LAYOUT proof; this card supplies the ACCESS proof and an executed layout OBSERVATION, and the honest reading is not to conflate them) and EXAMPLES-AGGREGATES (a published examples/records/ family - see EXAMPLES-SUITE-O). One measurement-hygiene finding is published rather than hidden, because it cost a full workspace run: a gitignored baseline tree extracted under measure/ is nonetheless VISIBLE TO A TEST THAT WALKS THE FILESYSTEM, and a whole-tree census test saw four .qcore files where it pins two. named_followups.title: The quantitative error region has a source path; thirteen residuals, and the operation variant was measured unreachable by design
named_followups.why: QUANT-REGION-SOURCE closes CT21/CT22's recorded gap - 'no source path emits RegionOp::QuantOpen' - and CORRECTS ITS OWN FRAMING IN THE PROCESS. source.region.v1 lands `error region NAME { ... } catch (ERROR) quant open NAME as BINDING { discharge BINDING; }` on the SEQUENTIAL route: it is not a route of its own and selects nothing, which is what gives it the existing certificate, reference execution, C emission and native comparison unchanged, and every other route keeps the refusal it already had (measured, not assumed). The sealed CleanupPack is bound as a LINEAR capability consumed EXACTLY ONCE - that linearity is the whole content of the word 'quant' here - and the region's body admits five kernel operations (Acquire, Drop, AddStrictCredit, SpendStrictCredit and the decided Raise), so this is NOT the open-plus-close-with-an-empty-interior fallback the card allowed for. ZERO reserved words (every word is already reserved and the shape already parsed, so the census is EXACT rather than statistical: before the card the statement collected R as a referenced name and refused at Q013, which means no program in this repository could contain it at all), ZERO new codes (Q302's condition widened to the reader's own shape refusals, with Q303-Q309 and Q300 reached from a second route at the codes that pass already allocates), NO new SourceOp, NO new CFG terminator and NO C backend rule. AN ADMITTED REGION ERASES FROM EMISSION: it compiles to byte-identical C with the hand-written straight-line program it is, measured three ways - a twin whose whole diff is the #line directive naming the other file, the emitted releases being the pack's duties in REVERSE (the model's own discharge cleanup trace), and a sanitized native run whose leak check is a POSITIVE control, since a discharge that lost a duty surfaces as an LSan leak rather than only as a disagreement. THE RECORDED GAP WAS MEASURED FALSE IN ONE HALF: RegionOp::QuantOpen, the operation VARIANT, is unreachable from a valid program BY DESIGN - its own doc comment says so - because the admitting constructor is the error_region::QuantOpen STRUCT on a catch clause, and the variant is retained so an opening outside a catch has an explicit Q302. The card lands the half that matters and names the other REGION-QUANTOPEN-OP-VARIANT rather than 'fixing' a refusal. The v1 PATH bound is deliberate and refused BY NAME rather than left silent, because analyze_error_regions calls handle_catch only for an error exit that reaches a matching clause, so a clause on a path the region does not take is a clause NOTHING DECIDES and admitting one would be silent rather than fail-closed. CT21 and CT22's ARCHIVED REASONS are retired - the opening and the credit both exist now, CT21 refusing at Q305 with two controls and CT22's credit half accepting with AbandonCredit(3) in the discharge's cleanup trace - while CT22 keeps a NARROWER gap in its scenario, 'after joins', which a lane must publish in its own stage-evidence record rather than carrying the archived one (constraint 23). The manifest is untouched and CT coverage does not move. 29 end-to-end tests, 8 unit tests, one new Lean module and audit whose load-bearing theorem produces the kernel's own discharge result and proves the emitted release sequence IS that result's cleanupTrace. Corpus-neutral. Standing constraint 15l records the erasure and the two do-not-repair rules. New: REGION-NORMAL-EXIT, REGION-MULTIPLE-CATCH, REGION-MULTIPLE, REGION-PROPAGATE, REGION-FAILING-ACQUIRE, REGION-IN-ARM, REGION-HANDLER-BODY, REGION-CATCH-PAYLOAD-BINDING and REGION-NESTED (each a refused shape with the capability it needs named - a multi-path region analysis, per-region diagnostic attribution, a second emission shape for a sealed pack leaving the entry, the handler's own statement vocabulary, four models that join a branch, the payload vocabulary), REGION-EFFECT-ROW (the sequential route has no effects syntax, so a region-carrying entry's Throws row is DERIVED from the module's declared error set - a boundary, not a claim), REGION-OUTER-LIVE-RESOURCES (a resource acquired outside the region contributes no RegionOp, so the model's ledger is a region-local view rather than the entry's), REGION-QUANTOPEN-OP-VARIANT (above) and REGION-CREDIT-WITH-JOINS (CT22's 'after joins' half - the same missing composition CT23-T07-SEAM names from the other side: credits on one route, error paths and joins on another).

By the user's ruling the presented coordinate is now the ORIGINAL, pre-preprocessing file:line (L19357 is flb_input_chunk.c:2267) and the preprocessed number stays INTERNAL - pin identity, leaf identity, certificate comparability. The map pairs the analysed -E -P text with a second, presentation-only MARKED -E run through the same marker reader legacy_enumeration has used since E01-TAIL, and the pairing is CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED: same length and same trimmed text line for line, or the whole map is refused. The anti-forgery property is stronger than 'hard to forge' - NO PRESENTED FILE SPELLING IS EVER READ FROM A FLAGLESS MARKER - and rests on three rules: a frame's spelling is adopted only from an ENTERING marker, so a #line, which Clang re-emits flagless, can never write one; include depth 0 is not named by a marker at all but resolved by the caller against the audit's own configured file; and a disagreeing flagless marker WITHDRAWS the coordinate for every line it governs rather than relabelling it, the diagnostic falling back to 'preprocessed line N', which names itself as internal. Proved in general as presented_files_are_entered_files (QCore.SourceCoordinate, one new audit file), with both measured #line directions of E01-TAIL pinned against real preprocessings. Standing constraint 12 is untouched: the scope reader is not read, not written and cannot be influenced, and the map is built only AFTER a unit's result is settled. Four fail-closed grounds all carry ReasonCategory::EnvironmentUnavailable on the producer-supplied path, so SS L21.1 rule 1 applies and none can contribute to a provisional Unsafe; a refused unit keeps every internal position and is never given an approximate coordinate. THE RE-PIN IS PRESENTATION-ONLY AND MEASURED TO BE: a fresh Clang pin, both runs reading the same 1,415-entry database, the BEFORE run reproducing the preceding baseline's diagnostics.json and chunk-contracts.json BYTE FOR BYTE, and the AFTER run compared leaf by leaf by the card's own oracle at ZERO STOP findings - 185 units, 4,834 functions, 54,383 diagnostics each with the same (function, preprocessed line, category), every unit key but functions and origin_coordinates byte-identical, every function row's status unchanged, leak 266, unknown_alias 4,344 and unsupported 49,773 all unmoved, and four of the five artifacts byte-identical between the two runs. What moved: 54,371 rows gained an origin, 266 descriptions had their SITE substituted (exactly the leak leaves - the only category here whose text names one, each rewrite verified to leave the text on both sides byte-identical), 178 unit rows gained an origin_coordinates account and two envelope keys changed. ZERO withdrawn lines and ZERO refused derivations across the corpus, so the anti-forgery rules are load-bearing for the PROPERTY rather than for the numbers. Spot checks read each coordinate back out of the pinned checkout by hand, reproducing the wave-22/23 records' :2483 and :2623 oracles and a deterministic cross-library sample. The corpus baseline moves to docs/reports/gateway-c-location/artifacts/; the preceding archives stay frozen. New: GATEWAY-LOCATION-LINE-ONLY-DIRECTIVE (a #line with no file spelling renumbers the file it is written in and is indistinguishable from one of Clang's own resynchronisations, which it must be, or every file with an #if 0 block would lose its coordinate; it moves no file identity, no include depth and no audited scope, and is the directive's C11 SS 6.10.4 meaning), GATEWAY-LOCATION-CONTRACT-TEXT (contract-text locations are out of scope BY THE USER'S RULING for this card), GATEWAY-LOCATION-INTERNAL-CHANNELS (the certificate, source-effects.json, chunk-contracts.json, the census APIs and the probe examples keep the preprocessed position - the user's ruling, not an omission), GATEWAY-LOCATION-INPUT-IDENTITY-REFUSAL (two unit-level refusal texts still name a preprocessed or input line; they fire BEFORE any analysis, where no map exists and no unit row is published, and one is additionally pinned by a qcore-schemas test), GATEWAY-LOCATION-SYNTHETIC-EXIT (12 leak rows sit at the synthetic preprocessed line 0 and carry origin null; giving a synthetic exit a coordinate would mean CHOOSING one, which this card will not do - their text still names the acquisition's original coordinate), GATEWAY-LOCATION-UNSAFE-REPREPROCESS (the Unsafe arm carries no preprocessed text and re-runs validate_unrestricted_c11 to obtain the authoritative bytes rather than accept a text derived another way; adding the field would touch 37 match sites), GATEWAY-LOCATION-SECOND-PREPROCESS (one extra marked -E run per unit with diagnostics; the enumeration already holds that output and could hand it over, but changing its shape touches the pinned denominator route - E01-TAIL-COST-DOUBLE-PP from the presentation side) and GATEWAY-LOCATION-HEADER-REACH (the header arm is exercised only by a fixture, because the pinned route's MainSourceDefinitions scope puts all 54,371 presented coordinates at depth 0).

named_followups.title: A hand edit to a carried matrix section can leave the derived count beside it stale
named_followups.why: Measured by card CT-WIRE-LANE-4 (wave 32) while taking constraint 25's clobber question seriously rather than assuming it. The committed matrix's dimensions.named_followups read 39 against 40 rows actually present in the carried named_followups section: commit 1c7d8e45 added the TRACE-ALPHABET-LEASE-REFUSAL-UNEXERCISED row by hand and did not move the derived count beside it, so the file was INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT between regenerations and nothing checked the pair. Tracing that produced a second consequence of the same edit: the file was also reserialized to the pre-HYGIENE-16 indent=2 format, having matched the generator's own indent=1 output at d31a8dc3, b5838915 and the wave-31 close -- so commit 1c7d8e45 wrote this file OUTSIDE ITS GENERATOR, and the next regenerating lane inherits an unreviewably large whole-file diff, as CT-WIRE-LANE-4 did. This lane's regeneration repairs both. The general shape stands as the residual: `dimensions` is DERIVED (`counted from the emitted rows`) while `named_followups`, `requirements` and the other hand-maintained sections are CARRIED, so any hand edit to a carried section can silently desynchronise a derived count and drift the file's format, with nothing checking either in between. Discharge: a check that compares each derived dimension against the carried section it counts -- the same shape as HYGIENE-14's repair of the bucket tally -- plus a format assertion, or a stated decision that hand edits are expected here and the counts advisory between regenerations. PARTIALLY DISCHARGED by card STABILITY-REEVAL-1 (wave 34), and narrowed rather than closed. scripts/tests/test_build_matrix_sections.py gains class CommittedMatrixIsSelfConsistent with two tests against the COMMITTED matrix - which is the gap, since the two pre-existing tests compare generator output against generator output, both self-consistent by construction, so neither could ever see drift in the committed file. That is why this residual fired twice and was caught both times by a person. test_each_derived_dimension_matches_the_section_it_counts covers the two dimensions whose name IS a section name (requirements, named_followups); test_the_committed_matrix_keeps_the_generators_byte_format covers the second half, a hand edit in another serialisation - the exact condition of commit 1c7d8e45, which buried a single real line in a 12,673-line reserialisation diff. Both were shown non-vacuous by mutation: setting dimensions.named_followups to 45 (the exact historical drift) turns the first red, and re-serialising at indent=2 turns the second red; the matrix was restored and verified byte-identical by sha256 afterwards. STILL OPEN: the derived cell and product counts (requirement_evidence_cells, ct_cells, ct_rows, unverified_spec_items), which this card deliberately left alone because each needs its own derivation rule and a wrong one would pin a wrong number.

named_followups.title: `return CALL(args)` with a non-neutral contract or summary is withdrawn, with its measurement published
named_followups.why: Card C-GATEWAY-RETURN-POSITION (wave 33) offered two sub-shapes and landed one. Sub-shape B - apply a callee's declared contract or validated W4 summary at a return position - is WITHDRAWN, and the grounds are measured over the real population rather than sampled. Of the 335 `return CALL(...)` leaves among the 511 functions the baseline blocks on the return position alone, only 12 (3.6%) name a callee with a declared contract; 94 name a callee the corpus already reports as uncontracted elsewhere and 227 name one declared nowhere, so for 323 of 335 clearing the return refusal would merely EXCHANGE it for a `call to uncontracted function` leaf and decide nothing. A cross-cut by whether W4 could derive a summary at all puts 236 of 335 (70.5%) in the unit's own .c and 99 outside it. Note also that a call whose contract is all-Borrowed with result None is ALREADY admitted today through admitted_neutral_call, so B's real content is narrower than it sounds. The soundness cost is decisive: applying a callee's Consumed/Released parameter mode at a return position would DISCHARGE a live obligation of the caller at that exit - invariant 1's forbidden direction - on a route whose observe_exit has no arm for a call result at all, constructing ReturnedValue only from EscapeIfOwned/Escape. Discharge: a card that lands a return-position effectful instruction together with its ReturnedValue construction, the matching summary validation and the certificate recheck, and that states up front how many functions it DECIDES rather than how many refusals it converts. Its decisive population today is 12.

named_followups.title: Most pure field-chain returns are refused by member typing, and the cost is unmeasured per premise
named_followups.why: Card C-GATEWAY-RETURN-POSITION (wave 33) admitted a pointer-valued bounded typed access chain in a `return` and moved 33 of the 511 return-only-blocked functions (6.5%). The natural candidate population is the 75 pure field-chain returns the card's whole-population census measured, of which only 31 are admitted. The remainder fail on F4 premises the card must not weaken: the member is not typed EXACTLY `struct TAG *` (a `char *`, a `cfl_sds_t`, a typedef the reader will not resolve, a `void *`), the record is incomplete, a union or has more than one definition in the unit, or the base is bound because it is named in some call's argument list elsewhere in the body. Discharge: measure, PER REFUSED PREMISE, how many functions a widened member typing would decide - PREDICTED BEFORE IT IS ATTEMPTED, as AOM-POISON-CONDITION-FRAME's discharge condition requires - and only then decide whether any premise can be widened without losing the base-premise argument the wave-33 admission rests on. That argument is that an admitted chain names no place the projection binds; a premise that weakens the base is not a typing change but a soundness change, and must land RETURN-POSITION-ESCAPE-UNREACHABLE's test in the same card.

named_followups.title: Conditional-expression returns are unmeasured as a population
named_followups.why: Card C-GATEWAY-RETURN-POSITION (wave 33) measured the whole 511-function return-only-blocked population by returned-expression shape and found 28 leaves (5.2%) are conditional expressions over field reads - `return error ? error->code : RD_KAFKA_RESP_ERR_NO_ERROR;` and the like. These refuse today for their OPERANDS rather than for the conditional operator itself: `?` and `:` are admitted operand punctuation, so a conditional all of whose operands are F4 chains or scalars is already admitted by the wave-33 rule, and the card's own re-pinned test drives exactly that shape. Discharge: measure how many of the 28 would be admitted if every operand were an F4 chain, which separates 'refused for the conditional' from 'refused for an untyped member' and tells a later card whether there is a population here at all. This is a measurement request, not a proposed widening.

named_followups.title: A fresh worktree starts without third_party/libevent and nothing forces the init before a gate
named_followups.why: AGENTS.md's standing gate opens with `git submodule update --init --recursive`, described as once per checkout, and invariant 5 pins the submodule revision with a test that fails if it is absent or moved. A delegated card's worktree is a fresh checkout, so the step is due every time and is enforced only by each agent remembering it. Wave 33 lost work to this twice: C-GATEWAY-RETURN-POSITION reported the libevent pin gate firing at the END of an audit run and costing it a full BEFORE run, and the integrator's own first gate on the VERIFIER-HOST-CLOSED-INPUT-DEADLINE candidate reported 10 failures - the revision pin plus every libevent census and header test - all of which vanished after the init, with 4,544 passed / 0 failed. Two independent hits in one wave is a process defect rather than bad luck, and the cost is asymmetric: the failure surfaces late and reads like a regression. Discharge: make the gate self-check the submodule before it runs anything expensive, or have worktree creation do the init, so a defective checkout cannot be mistaken for a defective change.

named_followups.title: The invariant that keeps a known non-null pointee-less pointer from arising holds at all fourteen write sites and is asserted nowhere
named_followups.why: This card asked whether an AbstractPointer can be inserted with targets empty, unknown false and may_be_null false - a claim of a known, non-null, pointee-less pointer that downstream readers could take as resolved. ANSWER: NO, measured by exhaustive enumeration of every construction, insertion, join and in-place mutation in legacy_c.rs. The invariant is targets.is_empty() implies (unknown || may_be_null). It holds at all six struct literals, the clone insertion, all three join arms, and every write to the two booleans; the single non-literal unknown=false site (:7887) immediately sets may_be_null (:7888), and the load-bearing may_be_null=false site (:7890) is guarded at :7880 by unknown || targets.len() > 1, so an empty-targets binding reaching it had unknown true. But the invariant is asserted NOWHERE - no doc comment on the struct (legacy_c.rs:5257-5263), no debug_assert, no Lean - and it rests on two conjuncts a plausible well-intentioned edit would remove: widening the :7880 guard to 'also narrow the empty case', which reads like a completeness fix and makes :7890 produce the triple directly; and replacing the Infeasible early return at :7893-7898 with a fallthrough. DISCHARGE: state the invariant as a doc comment on AbstractPointer and enforce it at a single insertion helper with a debug_assert, and name it in constraint 10b beside 'Non-nullness does not establish lookup identity'. Cheap, and JOINED-PROVENANCE-CALL-FRAMES will be editing next door.

named_followups.title: AbstractPointer derives Default and its Default is exactly the triple the invariant forbids
named_followups.why: legacy_c.rs:5257 derives Default on AbstractPointer { targets, unknown, may_be_null }, so AbstractPointer::default() IS targets empty / unknown false / may_be_null false - the triple POINTER-EMPTY-TARGETS-INVARIANT-UNSTATED shows must never reach state.pointers. It does not today: the two AbstractPointer::default() uses at :6649 and :6652 are local temporaries handed to mark_unresolved_effect and discarded, and there is no state.pointers.entry(..).or_default() anywhere. But or_default() is the idiomatic Rust one-liner and is already used six times in this same file on the neighbouring field_links, contained and conditional_replacements maps, so a future entry(name).or_default() on pointers would insert the forbidden triple silently, with no compile error and no test failure. DISCHARGE: remove the Default derive and spell the two temporaries as explicit literals. Do NOT discharge it by making the default unknown: true - that would silently change those two temporaries' behaviour, since mark_unresolved_effect with unknown true marks EVERY resource, an accusing change needing its own re-pin.

named_followups.title: The native comparison compares the logged event sequence, not the C operations beneath it; three mutations escaped before the repair
named_followups.why: Measured by card MUTEX-SHARE-CROSS-EMISSION (wave 36) and published rather than smoothed over, because it is the STABILITY-REEVAL shape found inside the card's own new evidence. CT46's sanitized native run compares the emitted program's stdout byte for byte with interpret_mutex_program's observation, and that stdout is produced by the typed diagnostic sink -- so it is evidence about the LOGGED sequence. Three mutations of the emitted C therefore ran byte-identical, exit 0, clean under ASan/UBSan/LSan: (a) deleting the real mtx_lock while keeping its log line; (b) moving the real mtx_unlock away from its log line; (c) calling the child function directly instead of thrd_create. Two repairs landed in the same card rather than a caveat: run_mutex_crossing now asserts on the EMITTED TEXT that every logged mutex event is immediately preceded by its own mtx_lock/mtx_unlock call -- the adjacency one renderer writes, proved as QCore.MutexShareCrossEmission.a_logged_acquisition_is_preceded_by_a_real_one -- and the thread boundary is pinned by emitted_c_contains plus a main_excludes check. With those, (a), (b) and (c) go red. WHAT REMAINS: the adjacency check covers the mutex operations only. A dropped payload WRITE is caught for a different reason -- the following read's sum is computed by C and would move -- but that is an accident of this fixture's shape, not a rule, and no equivalent structural check exists for touch/log pairs. DISCHARGE: extend the adjacency assertion to every (operation, log) pair the emitter writes, and drive each with its own emitter mutation; or state the non-mutex pairs as a measured boundary with the reason each is caught by something else.

named_followups.title: A typed-error exit inside a child refuses, because the model gives a child's exit status no meaning at the join
named_followups.why: Card MUTEX-SHARE-CROSS-EMISSION (wave 36) admits a non-nested fork/join mutex trace and refuses one whose child segment carries a MutexInvariantEvent::ErrorExit, classified Outside at the segment's own Spawn. The ground is that CheckedMutexInvariantV1 gives a child's typed-error exit no meaning AT THE JOIN: the emitted child function would have to return a status, and the creator would have to do something with it, and neither is anything the model decides. Rendering one would therefore invent semantics, so the arm fails closed instead. The refusal is driven by a hand-built trace in crates/qcore-core/tests/unit/mutex_c_emit.rs and shown non-vacuous by mutation, and it is proved in QCore.MutexShareCrossEmission (a_child_error_exit_is_refused). Whether it is reachable from SOURCE was not measured: lower_child_task refuses a typed-error exit at a child's top level, so reaching it needs one inside a `with lock` in the child's body. DISCHARGE: give the model a meaning for a child's error exit at the join and render it, or measure the source-level reachability and record the arm as a justified backstop, as MUTEX-SHARE-CROSS-ARMS did for its arms C and D.

named_followups.title: CT46's fork/join rendering has had no MSVC run, and none is claimed
named_followups.why: Card MUTEX-SHARE-CROSS-EMISSION (wave 36) compiles and runs CT46's own emitted C under ASan/UBSan/LSan on LINUX only. The manifest's four flipped stages are gated linux/macos for the run and linux/macos/windows for the emission, exactly as the route's existing sanitized runner is, and the emitted program's thread operations go through the embedded c11_threads_compat.h whose Windows arm is the winpthreads subset. No cl.exe or clang-cl run of a fork/join mutex program has happened, so no Windows claim is made -- the SLICE-PERMISSIONS-WINDOWS-RUN / WRITE-LEND-TASKS-WINDOWS-RUN precedent, and MSVC ships no ASan/UBSan in this harness in any case. DISCHARGE: run compiler/tests/ct_corpus.rs::ct_manifest_and_fixture_set_agree_and_mapped_cases_execute on a Windows host with the emitted CT46 program compiled by cl.exe, and record the byte comparison; the sanitizer half stays unclaimed there by construction.

named_followups.title: CT46's fork/join rendering has had no macOS run, and none is claimed
named_followups.why: The Apple sibling of MUTEX-SHARE-CROSS-EMISSION-WINDOWS-RUN. Card MUTEX-SHARE-CROSS-EMISSION (wave 36) gates CT46's native and sanitized stages linux/macos and the harness compiles the same file on both, but only the Linux arm was exercised. The macOS arm additionally differs in two recorded ways: Apple's AddressSanitizer implements no LeakSanitizer, so the harness forces detect_leaks=0 there and the reclamation of the protected allocation would be unwitnessed; and C11 threads reach Apple Clang through the pthread-backed subset. DISCHARGE: run the CT corpus on a macOS host and record which half of the Linux evidence reproduces -- byte comparison yes, leak detection no, on the EVENT-V1-APPLE-RUN precedent.

named_followups.title: The worker-side lease exercise's native test ran the Linux arm only; no Windows or Apple run is claimed
named_followups.why: Card WRITE-LEND-TASKS-EXERCISE (wave 36) landed the worker-side range write and its sanitized native comparison: two threads writing distinct bytes of one int32_t payload under ASan/UBSan/LSan, native stdout byte-identical to the reference execution's own rendering, one allocation released once. That run is LINUX. The macOS arm compiles the same test file (the Apple threads shim include is wired) but was not executed here, and no MSVC run has happened at all. The tests/support/windows_c.rs path is carried UNCHANGED by this card - the emitted difference is two new preamble helpers and two diagnostic kinds, neither platform-specific - so this is an unexercised arm rather than a suspected one, on the WRITE-LEND-TASKS-WINDOWS-RUN and STRING-CONCAT-WINDOWS-RUN precedent. No Windows or Apple claim is made or implied anywhere in the card's report or in standing constraint 15h's appendix. CONDITION: a Windows run of two_threads_write_disjoint_bytes_of_one_object_sanitized that compiles the emitted C with cl.exe, executes it, and compares stdout byte for byte with the reference rendering; and an Apple run of the same test.

named_followups.title: A program mixing whole-payload and byte access has a host-dependent observation, because the payload's object representation is
named_followups.why: Card WRITE-LEND-TASKS-EXERCISE (wave 36) made the worker's byte write a write to a real byte of the emitted struct qcore_buffer's int32_t payload - ((unsigned char *)&buffer->payload)[index] - deliberately, because that and only that makes two workers' writes DISTINCT MEMORY LOCATIONS under C11 6.2.6.1/4 and 3.14 and therefore not a data race. A value-level read-modify-write of the whole payload was considered and REJECTED for exactly that reason, not for cost. The consequence is that the relation between a byte at index i and the int32 value is the host's object representation. The reference execution models the same representation (i32::to_ne_bytes), so reference and emitted C AGREE ON EVERY HOST and nothing here is unsound; what is host-dependent is a published TRANSCRIPT of a program that mixes whole-payload and byte access. The card's flagship is representation-independent BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by luck: C11 7.20.1.1 makes int32_t two's complement with no padding bits, so the initial value 0 has an all-zero representation on every conforming host, and a byte written at index i and read back at index i is the same byte whatever the order of the four. The route admits the mixed programs with this boundary stated rather than refusing them, because refusing would need per-buffer byte-write history the checker does not carry. CONDITION: either commit the route to a byte order at the reference/emission boundary, or refuse a whole-payload access on a buffer with byte-write history - whichever a later card measures to be cheaper - and say which programs each choice costs.

named_followups.title: The owner has no byte write: the whole-payload write remains its only write footprint, deliberately
named_followups.why: Card WRITE-LEND-TASKS-EXERCISE (wave 36) gave a LEASE HOLDER a byte write and deliberately did not give one to the owner, and the reason is a dependency rather than a preference. Card WRITE-LEND-TASKS' rule that 'the owner holds no whole-payload authority, read included, while any lease is out' is stricter than both the read-share route and the sequential lend's per-byte exclusion, and standing constraint 15h states WHY in one clause: because the owner's only spellable footprint here is the whole payload. Admitting an owner byte write would introduce a second owner-side footprint that rule was never measured against, and would immediately raise a question the route has no answer to - whether an owner byte write OUTSIDE every live lease is admitted, which is an ADMITTING direction and so needs the per-byte owner exclusion the ledger does not currently compute. The refusal is in the IR and driven by its own test (the_ir_refuses_an_owner_byte_write), not only by the frontend's earlier message. The owner's byte READ is admitted, and takes the same ledger gate its whole-payload read takes, so a lease outstanding refuses it by the existing rule. CONDITION: a card that wants an owner byte write must re-measure wave 31's whole-payload suspension against a second owner-side footprint and land the per-byte owner exclusion, with the disjointness decided by ownership::axes_overlap as everywhere else.

named_followups.title: A read share admits the whole-payload read and no byte view
named_followups.why: Card WRITE-LEND-TASKS-EXERCISE (wave 36) admits a byte read through a write lease (relative to its low) and through an owner (absolute), and refuses one through a borrow<Buffer> read share by name, in the IR, driven by its own test (the_ir_refuses_a_byte_read_through_a_read_share) as well as by the frontend's earlier message. The refusal is fail-closed and cheap to keep: a read share is a COUNTED share of the whole payload, and giving it a byte view would need a cross-model rule relating share counts to byte ranges that no model in the tree states. Nothing is blocked by the refusal today - the whole-payload read a share already admits is strictly more information than any byte of it. CONDITION: a card that wants byte-granular read shares supplies the rule relating counted shares to ranges, on the sequential route's read-loan overlap precedent (constraint 15h: two overlapping BORROWS are deliberately not refused, because both are immutable and conflict on nothing), and shows it non-vacuous in both directions.

named_followups.title: A range write lease's bounds live in [0, 4) because the task route's Buffer payload is one int32_t
named_followups.why: Introduced by card WRITE-LEND-TASKS (wave 31) and NOT discharged by WRITE-LEND-TASKS-EXERCISE (wave 36), which makes it more valuable rather than less. BUFFER_PAYLOAD_BYTES is 4 - the real bytes of the emitted struct qcore_buffer's int32_t payload - so every lease of this route is a sub-range of four bytes and a two-worker disjoint split is two bytes each. Wave 36 turned that from a permission into a demonstration: two threads really do write distinct bytes of one object under the sanitizers. But four bytes is a thin demonstration, and the interesting cases for disjoint concurrent writing - a split buffer worked on by several workers, a chunked fill - are all out of reach until a byte-extent buffer (bytes(N)) can cross a spawn. Recorded here because wave 36's report names it and no tracker held it. CONDITION: as wave 31 stated it - a bytes(N) buffer crossing a spawn boundary, with the lease bounds decided against that extent rather than against the int32 payload, and the emitted C carrying the real allocation.

named_followups.title: A sole-blocker cover is an upper bound on function moves, never a forecast
named_followups.why: A refusal reachable only after the first one is removed is invisible to a cover built from emitted leaves: it cost card W36-CORPUS-CONTRACTS-3 three of its 23 predicted function moves, the cJSON_Delete trio exchanging its decided leaf for a `nested call ... inside a modeled call` refusal that was unreachable while the outer call was uncontracted. This bounds what any future cover card may promise. DISCHARGE: a cover modelling the projection's reachability, not only its emitted leaves.

named_followups.title: Three cJSON functions exchanged a decided leaf for a nested-call refusal
named_followups.why: The three cJSON functions W36-CORPUS-CONTRACTS-3 predicted would move did not: each exchanged its decided leaf for `nested call ... inside a modeled call`. DISCHARGE: nested-call-in-argument-position admission, or W4 summaries for the three `cJSON_DetachItemFrom*` callees, which are in the same unit.

named_followups.title: W4 derives Released{nonnull} where the faithful declaration says nullable
named_followups.why: The corpus's first `summary_conflict` (0 -> 1), and it costs `rd_kafka_mem_free` its own Safe. The declaration is the faithful one - `rd_free(NULL)` reaches `free(NULL)` - and declaring `nonnull` to silence the conflict would assert a precondition the body does not have (constraint 4), so this is constraint 8's gate working in the conservative direction and not a defect. It is still a live W4 defect with a concrete repair. DISCHARGE: a W4 derivation that reads a delegate's declared nullability instead of defaulting a released formal to `nonnull`.

named_followups.title: 26 sites still refuse arguments beyond mk_print's declared parameters
named_followups.why: The `resource_variadic_data_tail()` clause admits nothing on its own, as designed, so 26 sites keep the `arguments beyond the declared parameters of mk_print` refusal. DISCHARGE: a per-site tail-actual admission, or acceptance as a measured boundary.

named_followups.title: cJSON_Delete releases a reachable set; v1 can only state the fact about one parameter
named_followups.why: `cJSON_Delete` releases the whole `next` chain and the subtree beneath it; the declaration states the fact about `item` alone, so the corpus carries a declaration weaker than the C. named_followups.title: `add` cannot be declared: three definitions, three signatures, one of them static inline
named_followups.why: Declined by W36-CORPUS-CONTRACTS-3 because the pinned corpus carries three distinct definitions of `add` with three signatures, the cmetrics one `static inline` with no header declaration, and a `.qcore` declaration is corpus-wide. DISCHARGE: a unit-scoped declaration vocabulary, which v1 has none of; W4 summary inference is the right lever meanwhile. RESTATED by card W37-CORPUS-CONTRACTS-4 (wave 37, section 10 item 10; applied at the wave-37 close in the card's words): the rule is about definitions that DISAGREE, not about several definitions. Four identical vendored copies are safe to declare; three copies with three signatures are not. Without that refinement the rule would have declined that card's largest module.

named_followups.title: contract/qcore/ctraces/ is a new family whose convention is one card's choice
named_followups.why: The family has one module. Its manifest placement (after `cmetrics/`, before `monkey/`) and the module name `context_lifetime.qcore`, paired with cmetrics' identically-named sibling, are W36-CORPUS-CONTRACTS-3's choice alone and no convention was found to follow. named_followups.title: The sixth constraint-16 row measured failing at mid-range load, after its repair
named_followups.why: `closed_input_does_not_mask_descendant_timeout_or_accept_a_partial_request` (crates/qcore-verifier-host/tests/standalone_host.rs:175) failed once inside a full gate at load average ~40 on 16 cores and passed 12/12 in isolation at load 23.7 to 27.6. This is the row's first measurement at the MIDDLE of the load range - wave 35 measured it at ~100 and at ~6.5 - and it is post-poll(2)-repair, so the repair narrows the failure window without closing it. The card proposed the measurement as ADDING a sixth row; the row had been the sixth since the wave-35 close, so the WAVE-36-CLOSE declined that half and landed the measurement beside the existing row instead. DISCHARGE: the 1s wall-clock bound is pinned against a measured margin, or the repair is reopened - never by weakening the bound.

named_followups.title: Two over-approximations of constraint 5's one sentence disagree on 16% of the family
named_followups.why: `FunctionTypes::may_bind` (bound_names) and `UntrackedBases::never_bound` (untracked_bases) disagree on 2,933 leaves (16.0%): 2,893 where may_bind says the base is bindable and never_bound says it is not, and 40 the other way. Constraint 5's wording is may_bind's, and may_bind is the stricter refuser here, so a card reading never_bound works in a space roughly FOUR TIMES larger than the constraint describes without saying so. Neither function is defective; they are consumed by different rules. It is a trap for any wave-37 arbiter. DISCHARGE: state in constraint 5 which reading the premise names, or prove the two agree wherever an admission consults them.

named_followups.title: One unparsable member declaration makes every member of that record unclassifiable
named_followups.why: `TypedAccessModel::read_record_body` refuses a whole record body on any '(', ')', '{', '}', ':' or '=', so 173 of 909 record tags (19.0%) in the pinned corpus are refused wholesale - 98 on '{', 66 on '(', 9 on ':' - accounting for 2,713 unresolved-member leaves. The one genuine CODE DEFECT the census found, filed on its own merits. It is NOT a promising arbiter: the measured ceiling is 2 sole-blocked functions, 1 with constraint 5's premise intact. DISCHARGE: a per-member total-or-reject reader - classify the member declarations that parse, mark the ones that do not as explicitly unreadable so they stay refused - landed with its own measured re-pin, or a recorded decision that the 2-function reach does not justify the risk. NOT A DISCHARGE: citing the 2,713 leaves. SECOND MEASURED VALUE, card BASE-TYPE-READER-CENSUS (wave 37, sections 6.2 and 11.2; recorded at the wave-37 close): the two-function ceiling is the STANDALONE number. Beside the base-type reader's Rank 1 repair the same repair is worth five more functions, because 41.6% of Rank 1's leaves land on a record body refused whole. A repair worth 2 alone and 5 in company is a different proposition; the disposition itself (declined as a standalone arbiter) is a wave-38 cut decision and is not changed here.

named_followups.title: Admitting an access can move counts in the admitting direction for unrelated reasons
named_followups.why: A cross-cutting soundness hazard for every admission candidate, and the one most easily missed. Admitting an access makes its statement no longer refused, so that statement's RefusedWrites no longer poisons any binding. Constraint 10a already records that sparing a binding can UNMASK a stale scalar fact a NoOp mutation left behind (AOM-POISON-NOOP-INCREMENT: `pass++` lowering to NoOp so a Clear-bound scalar stays definitely-null for ever, making a `pass != 0` edge Infeasible and suppressing the refusals inside it). A wave-37 arbiter's re-pin can therefore move counts for reasons unrelated to the access it admits. DISCHARGE: the arbiter measures, for its own admitted set, how many refusals disappear through an edge becoming infeasible rather than through the access being modelled, and publishes the two numbers apart.

named_followups.title: A seventh test shows constraint 16's signature and is none of its six named rows
named_followups.why: `a_forced_override_never_weakens_an_execution` (crates/qcore-verifier-host/tests/execution_quota.rs:777) failed with Io("Broken pipe (os error 32)") in a workspace run deliberately concurrent with two pinned corpus audits, and passes in the card's isolated gate. That is constraint 16's exact signature and crate, but the test is not one of its six named rows nor the deliberately-excluded seventh. Filed rather than promoted: each constraint-16 row carries a measured load figure and one observation under a heavy self-inflicted load is not one. Named in constraint 16 by WAVE-36-CLOSE so the list is known incomplete rather than assumed complete. DISCHARGE: a card that bisects the load at which it flips, as vp04_vp07_vp08 was measured failing at 50 and passing at 37, and either adds the row with its figure or records that it is the same mechanism as an existing row. NOT A DISCHARGE: re-running until green.

named_followups.title: The Declaration arm's census reads a window the gate did not read
named_followups.why: For the 15 `Declaration`-arm leaves the gate's predicate is not `contains_unmodeled_access` but a separate bracket/dot test over the declaration prefix, so the census reads a different window from the gate. 15 leaves of 18,555; recorded rather than repaired. DISCHARGE: give the declaration arm its own census window, or state the arm is out of every arbiter's scope and drop the axis for it.

named_followups.title: One published leaf of 18,555 is explained by no census statement
named_followups.why: 0.01% of the family. The likeliest cause is the `for`-clause path: `classify_simple` is also called for a `for` init and increment clause, where the statement the parser attributes is the `for`'s own line rather than the clause's first token, so the census's (function, line) key can miss. Not chased, because it is one leaf and the direction is understood. DISCHARGE: thread the statement's attributed line into `classify_simple` rather than reading it off the first token, and re-run; or identify the leaf and record why it is unexplainable.

named_followups.title: CT10-REASON-ROW and MATRIX-UPDATED-STALE-AT-WAVE-27 are now both a deferred decision and a named_followup
named_followups.why: Card STABILITY-REEVAL #2 registered both names in named_followups, correctly, because STABILITY-REEVAL #1 had raised them and no tracker carried them (STABILITY-REEVAL-1-RESIDUALS-ORPHANED). But both are ALSO open deferred decisions, carried from the wave-33 close through waves 34 and 35, and the wave-35 close's own classification says in terms that decisions 'must not be registered as followups as well'. Neither half is wrong on its own and the close did not undo either: --check re-lists them as decisions and --residuals now sees them tracked, so both mechanisms work. The hazard is at the END - resolving the decision will not retire the followup, and retiring the followup will not resolve the decision, so one half can stand for waves after the other is answered, which is the same silence the re-listing mechanism was landed to prevent. This is also the shape STABILITY-REEVAL #2 item 5 asks the close rule to cover from the other direction (retiring a tracker entry must re-home every name it was the sole tracker for). DISCHARGE: state which mechanism owns a name that is both, and add the cross-check to the close rule - or, if both are to be kept, make each entry name the other so ending one is visibly half the job. CT-REMAINING-IMPLEMENTATION resolves CT10-REASON-ROW in both its tracker retirement and its reconciliation deferred_decisions record. The next numbered wave close must carry that resolved decision because outstanding_decisions discovers only numbered close directories. The other names and the general dual-tracking mechanism remain open.

named_followups.title: 158 leaves of the dominant base-type cause name an anonymous aggregate, which no tag-resolving reader change can reach
named_followups.why: Introduced by BASE-TYPE-READER-CENSUS (wave 37). The card's Rank 1 reader change resolves TypedefTarget::Aggregate("struct TAG") to DeclaredType::Record(TAG). 158 of the cause's 3,220 leaves (4.9%) carry the head `struct` with NO tag - typedef struct { ... } t; - so there is nothing to resolve to; 33 more carry `union`, which must stay Opaque because a union member may overlap a pointer, and 4 carry `enum`. Reaching the anonymous ones needs a SYNTHETIC tag keyed on the typedef name, which is a new record identity that W4 derivation, W4 validation and certificate rechecking would all have to reproduce (constraint 8's both-readers rule). DISCHARGE: a card that lands the synthetic tag with its own measured re-pin, or a recorded measured decision that 158 leaves do not justify a new record identity. NOT a discharge: citing the 158 leaves, which is leaf mass and the error this family keeps inviting.

named_followups.title: The second discount could be applied to one of fourteen base-type causes, so the 47-function union is not comparable with the 12 and the 17
named_followups.why: Introduced by BASE-TYPE-READER-CENSUS (wave 37). Committing a base's declared type yields a record TAG, not an admission: the member must then classify and the access rule must then admit it. The card could test that second step for exactly ONE cause - TypedefDefinesAggregate, whose payload names the record - where it cut the cleared set from 30 to 12. Every other cause's CLEAR column in the card's section 6.1 still carries the untested assumption, so the union figure of 47 functions and the per-cause figures of 5, 3, 2, 2, 2, 1, 1 and 1 are upper bounds on upper bounds and must not be added to or compared with the 12 and the 17. DISCHARGE: stream the tag a committed base WOULD have yielded for the remaining causes and re-run the second discount, or state per cause that the question cannot be asked and why.

named_followups.title: The census's file-scope name table under-reports, so the FileScopeDeclaration / Unknown split is approximate in one direction
named_followups.why: Introduced by BASE-TYPE-READER-CENSUS (wave 37). To separate `this unit declares the base at file scope` (161 leaves) from `nothing declares it anywhere the census can see` (69 leaves), the card builds a file-scope name table using the SAME is_declaration_candidate / statement_end / read_declaration reader the function bodies use - deliberately, because a second reader here would be the mistake the census exists to avoid. The consequence is that a file-scope declaration that reader will not read is absent from the table and its name is reported Unknown, so the split under-reports FileScopeDeclaration. Neither cause decides more than one function, so nothing in the card's recommendation turns on it. DISCHARGE: measure the gap against a Clang-derived file-scope set, or record the axis as bounded in the refusing direction and stop splitting it.

named_followups.title: C-GATEWAY-INDIRECT-CENSUS-2's 18,555 / 284 / 833 describe the corpus before its own wave's contract arbiter landed
named_followups.why: Measured by BASE-TYPE-READER-CENSUS (wave 37), which counts 18,549 family leaves, 285 sole-blocked functions and 835 sole-blocked leaves on the current baseline by the same method. The delta is attributed exactly rather than plausibly, by counting the family in each archived diagnostics.json.gz of the chain: c-gateway-constant-do-while, joined-provenance-cycles and w36-corpus-contracts-3's BEFORE all hold 18,555 / 284 / 833; w36-corpus-contracts-3's AFTER and both sides of joined-provenance-call-frames hold 18,549 / 285 / 835. Wave 36's FIRST, declarative arbiter decided six leaves of this family and moved one function INTO the sole-blocked set with two leaves; the wave's second arbiter moved this family by zero. Neither card is wrong and the frozen archives must not be edited (constraint 21). This is the first measured instance of the registered residual JPC-CENSUS-CONTRACT-SET-DEPENDENT, which is therefore confirmed rather than hypothetical. named_followups.title: The value route still deletes a loop header's BODY edge from a modelled value, on the same two unverifiable premises
named_followups.why: Card SCALAR-ROUTE-EXIT-EDGE (wave 37) restricted the EXIT direction of refine_pointer_null's Infeasible arm and deliberately left the sibling BACK edge alone. A positively spelled loop header - `while (flag)` with a known-null binding, `while (p)` with a known-non-null one - still loses its BODY edge, decided from a modelled value, on exactly the two premises the card found unverifiable: the volatile witness applies unchanged (a volatile zero flag with `while (flag) { q_free(p); q_free(p); }` was measured Safe, swallowing a double release INSIDE the body), and constraint 10a's Sparing completeness applies unchanged. It is not folded in because deleting a body edge is what C-GATEWAY-CONSTANT-DO-WHILE proved for a literal token, and CONSTANT-DO-WHILE-OTHER-CONSTANTS gives the ground for the mirror case: the other direction must not be folded into this rule. Measured corpus reach today: 0 of 201 loop-header BranchOnNull nodes delete a body edge. DISCHARGE: a card that either proves the back-edge deletion sound under a premise it states and the analyzer can check, or restricts it, in both cases with its own measured re-pin and a test driving a volatile flag and a spared body write.

named_followups.title: The gateway's abstract state assumes no asynchronous modification, and that premise is written down nowhere
named_followups.why: Card SCALAR-ROUTE-EXIT-EDGE (wave 37) measured a value-derived must-fact in legacy_c.rs to be FALSE for a volatile object: C11 5.1.2.3 lets such an object be modified by means outside the program, so `while (!flag) { }` on a volatile flag terminates in well-defined C while the abstract state still calls flag null. The reduced importer does not read the volatile qualifier, so every value-derived must-fact in the file inherits this premise silently - it is a global premise of the same kind as AOM-POISON-NO-UB (constraint 10a), which IS recorded, where this one is not. The card's restriction removes the premise's LOAD at a loop header's exit edge and nowhere else. DISCHARGE: a census of the places in legacy_c.rs where a value-derived must-fact decides an admission or a CFG edge, followed either by recording the premise as a standing constraint beside 5a and 10a with that census as its evidence, or by giving the importer the qualifier so the premise can be checked rather than assumed.

named_followups.title: 154 corpus branch-edge prunings rest on the same two premises and carry no theorem
named_followups.why: Card SCALAR-ROUTE-EXIT-EDGE (wave 37) deliberately preserved refine_pointer_null's branch pruning, measuring it at 154 corpus edges (24 through the empty_targets arm, 130 through known_non_null), because an `if`'s two arms rejoin at the same continuation so pruning one orphans no destination - that is the precision a blanket restriction would have destroyed. But a pruned arm's diagnostics are still not reported, and under the volatile witness a pruned arm CAN be taken. Whether any of the 205 corpus Safe functions depends on one is NOT measured by that card, which measured only that none depends on a deleted EXIT edge. DISCHARGE: re-run the card's census harness (docs/reports/scalar-route-exit-edge/scripts/) with branch pruning disabled and diff the verdicts, which answers the question the same way the card answered it for loop headers; then either prove the branch arm sound under a stated premise or record the measured dependence.

named_followups.title: The 'hazard unreached in the corpus' result is a coverage fact, and one card away from being false

named_followups.title: The value route's zero spellings do NOT move with CONSTANT-DO-WHILE-ZERO-SPELLINGS - measured, with the ground
named_followups.why: Card SCALAR-ROUTE-EXIT-EDGE (wave 37) was asked whether the value route's unclaimed zero spellings move with CONSTANT-DO-WHILE-ZERO-SPELLINGS, and measured that they do not. The two rules key DIFFERENT PREDICATES IN DIFFERENT POSITIONS: condition_is_literal_zero (legacy_c.rs:4652) matches a single token whose text is "0" over a CONDITION token stream, while the value route keys on is_null_constant (legacy_c.rs:4799), which matches NULL, nullptr, 0 and (void *)0, applied to an INITIALIZER's right-hand side and to the operands of == and !=. Neither is a subset of the other - is_null_constant already accepts two spellings condition_is_literal_zero refuses - so widening one does not widen the other, and CONSTANT-DO-WHILE-ZERO-SPELLINGS's discharge (a preprocessed census of do-while CONDITIONS) does not answer this question. Pinned by the_other_zero_spellings_reach_neither_arm: 0x0, 0u, 0L, 00, a null character constant and 1 - 1 bind no known null, reach neither deciding arm and keep every edge. DISCHARGE: a census of INITIALIZER right-hand sides over the 185 units classifying every single-token integer constant expression, followed either by a widening of is_null_constant with its own measured re-pin or by a recorded statement that the set is empty. Note the direction: widening is_null_constant would create new exit-edge deletions on this route, which is now harmless because card SCALAR-ROUTE-EXIT-EDGE refuses them whatever the binding says.

named_followups.title: The proved round bound's descent hypothesis is stated of, not proved of, the Rust transfer
named_followups.why: QCore.JoinedProvenanceRoundBound.rounds_are_bounded_by_the_graph_budget bounds the sweep by nodes * (1 + sites + sites * names) on the hypothesis that every non-fixed sweep strictly decreases the module's measure. It is an abstract rule theorem, not extraction (GATEWAY-LEAN-ABSTRACT-NOT-EXTRACTION): Facts::step's four arms, outgoing's conditional-name retain and the null-edge exclusion are premises, none proved monotone. The premise is not idle - the card records that the NAIVE measure (counting only stored names) makes a site's arrival INCREASE the count, so the obvious reading of the hypothesis is false and the correct one reads absence as the top of that site's own lattice. named_followups.title: fixed_point's declining arm is unreachable from derive unless the round-bound theorem is false, so no test drives it end to end

named_followups.title: The proved round bound buys sufficiency, not speed, and the cost of a graph that actually approached its bound is unmeasured
named_followups.why: Card JOINED-PROVENANCE-ROUND-BOUND (wave 37) measured corpus-wide sweep cost rising from 803,004 to 1,074,540 round-edge steps (+33.8%) when the cap became the per-graph proved bound - immeasurably small against a ~7-minute audit, and no graph comes near its own bound (the closest approach in the pinned corpus is set_events_from_ctr at 13 of 28, 46%). named_followups.title: The proved round bound exceeds the observed maximum by one to two orders of magnitude and no tighter bound is proved
named_followups.why: Over the 159 sweeping visits of the pinned corpus the proved bound nodes * (1 + sites + sites * names) runs min 28 / median 378 / max 17,091, against an observed maximum of 148 rounds (card JOINED-PROVENANCE-ROUND-BOUND, wave 37). For 11 of those 159 visits the proved bound is at or below the old constant of 64, so the old cap was already provably sufficient there and nobody knew. The classical tighter results for this shape - loop connectedness for a round-robin sweep in reverse postorder - do not carry to this Jacobi schedule unchanged, and none is proved here. Looseness costs nothing today because nothing approaches the loose bound; it is recorded so that a later cost question (JOINED-PROVENANCE-BOUND-COST-UNMEASURED) is not answered by tightening something nobody proved.
