named_followups.title: Every ThreadSanitizer row in this repository runs a pthread-bound build, not the published thread primitive
named_followups.why: Card TASK-ROUTE-TSAN (wave 37) found why no TSan row existed: ThreadSanitizer's runtime ships an interceptor for pthread_create and NONE for thrd_create, so on glibc 2.34+ a thread the emitted runtime creates reaches start_thread unregistered, cur_thread() is null in it, and the first instrumented event faults at __tsan_func_entry+19 (mov 0x18(%rdi),%rax) - the address 0x18 wave 36 recorded. That is a sanitizer-runtime gap and not a QCore defect, proved by a fifteen-line C file containing no QCore code which dies identically, and by its pthread twin which runs clean. Emitting C11 thrd_create is deliberate (the route must also emit for MSVC), so nothing in QCore was changed: tests/support/thread_sanitizer.rs replaces thrd_create/thrd_join AT THEIR CALL SITES through -include, changing ZERO emitted bytes, and the replacement bodies are the pthread-backed ones the shipped c11_threads_compat.h already compiles on Apple hosts. WHAT THIS COSTS, stated rather than elided: the program TSan observes differs from the published program in which symbol spawns the thread. It is not a different concurrency structure - glibc implements thrd_create by calling pthread_create's implementation, visible in the faulting backtrace itself, where the unbound worker's frame sits directly on start_thread at nptl/pthread_create.c:451 - so every happens-before edge TSan reasons about here is the same edge in both builds, and the one representation assumption (thrd_t and pthread_t are one representation) is a _Static_assert in the header rather than a comment. What the rows therefore CANNOT speak for is the thrd_create call itself and the Windows and Apple thread arms. DISCHARGE: re-run the rows with bind_threads=false and record them green, once a toolchain ships a thrd_create interceptor - which a_program_with_no_qcore_in_it_dies_the_same_way will announce by going red on the day it happens - or land a pthread emission mode and state what it costs portability.

named_followups.title: A clean ThreadSanitizer run is evidence about the schedules that ran, not a proof of race freedom
named_followups.why: Card TASK-ROUTE-TSAN (wave 37) landed the repository's first TSan rows and states their strength here so no later reader over-reads them. TSan is a happens-before detector, so it generalizes beyond the exact interleaving observed - it reports a race between two accesses it saw with no ordering edge between them, whatever order they happened to occur in - but it still only sees CODE PATHS THAT EXECUTED, on one machine, under one allocator, a handful of times. The rows are therefore evidence, not proof, and the card's own text says so. Two specific narrownesses: (1) each program is run ONCE per test, so a path taken only under a different allocation or spawn outcome is unobserved - the emitted programs' failure arms in particular (a failed qcore_buffer_new, a failed spawn) are never taken; (2) for CT46's crossing the checked trace SERIALISES the child, so the creator and child never contend, which MUTEX-SHARE-CROSS-EMISSION-NO-CONTENTION already owns and which this card's test restates in its own doc comment rather than quietly improving on. DISCHARGE: either state it permanently as a measured boundary (the current disposition), or drive the rows over the failure arms and over repeated runs, and say which schedules were covered. AMENDED by TSAN-ROWS-2 (wave 39): the second half of the discharge is met - every task-route subject runs 20 times per mutation under three named schedules (unforced; together, all created and released before any body runs and all threads live until all bodies have run; reverse, last-created first to completion), the realised schedule asserted from the harness trace - and the CT46 half is decided (serial by construction). What remains is the failure arms, carried as TSAN-FORCED-SCHEDULE-FAILURE-ARMS.

named_followups.title: The ThreadSanitizer rows ran the Linux arm only; no Windows or Apple TSan claim is made
named_followups.why: Card TASK-ROUTE-TSAN (wave 37) gates every one of its rows #[cfg(target_os = "linux")], and that is a real restriction rather than a formality: the diagnosis (glibc's thrd_create, TSan's missing interceptor), the binding and every measurement are x86-64-Linux/glibc observations. On any other platform the file contributes NO ROWS - it does not pass vacuously, which is the CT-COMPOSED-NATIVE-NON-LINUX-VACUOUS-PASS shape the card was told not to repeat, and the gating is stated in the file's own header. MSVC ships no ThreadSanitizer in this harness at all, and Apple's differs from Linux's in ways nothing here has measured; the emitted programs' thread operations reach those platforms through c11_threads_compat.h's winpthreads and pthread-backed arms, neither of which any TSan run has touched. On the MUTEX-SHARE-CROSS-EMISSION-WINDOWS-RUN / WRITE-LEND-EXERCISE-WINDOWS-RUN precedent. DISCHARGE: an Apple run of compiler/tests/task_route_tsan.rs with the cfg widened and the binding's _Static_assert re-checked there, recording which rows reproduce; the Windows half stays unclaimed by construction while no TSan ships for it.

named_followups.title: The correct TSan diagnosis existed in a report for several waves, reached no tracker, and was then contradicted by a later card
named_followups.why: A STABILITY-REEVAL-shaped process finding measured by card TASK-ROUTE-TSAN (wave 37) inside its own subject, and published rather than smoothed over. docs/reports/remaining-t04/README.md 5.1 already said, in these words, 'ThreadSanitizer does not intercept C11 thrd_create, and a -fsanitize=thread build of ANY emitted task program dies with SEGV on unknown address 0x18' - the correct diagnosis, together with the remedy this card eventually took ('adding a pthread emission mode purely for race testing, is recorded as open'). That open item was never registered as a residual: it is exactly the --residuals half of the reconciliation defect CLAUDE.md's close rule describes. The consequence was not merely delay. Wave 36's WRITE-LEND-TASKS-EXERCISE re-measured the symptom, added a minimal-program control that ran clean, and concluded the OPPOSITE attribution - 'so the fault is in what this route emits and not in the toolchain's C11 threads support' - which is how TASK-ROUTE-TSAN-SEGV came to be written against the route. Its control was a false negative: a thread body with no memory access and no call is not instrumented at all, so there is no __tsan_func_entry to fault, which this card pins as an_uninstrumented_body_is_why_the_minimal_probe_ran_clean. Note also that MUTEX-SHARE-CROSS-EMISSION-NO-CONTENTION's own text cites remaining-t04 for the correct diagnosis, so both readings were live in the tracker simultaneously and nothing compared them. DISCHARGE: at a close, sweep report sections for open items phrased as prose ('is recorded as open') rather than as named residuals, and either register or decline each - the sweep's --residuals arm finds names, not sentences, which is the gap this instance sits in.

named_followups.title: The declared-ABI reader parses a function-pointer TYPEDEF but not an INLINE function-pointer parameter declarator, and withdraws the declaration
named_followups.why: Card W37-CORPUS-CONTRACTS-4 (wave 37) declared `rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_sort`, its highest-yield callee at two projected functions. The loader WITHDREW it in every calling translation unit with `abi-unreadable-declaration`, so both targets stayed Unknown. The cause was diagnosed rather than guessed: `crates/qcore-c-gateway/src/legacy_declared_abi.rs` records that card CONSTRUCTOR-RESIDUALS-ABI-TYPEDEF taught the reader the function-pointer TYPEDEF shape, which is exactly why `msgpack_packer_init`'s `callback: fnptr` works (its C parameter is `msgpack_packer_write callback`, a named typedef, at lib/msgpack-c/include/msgpack/pack.h:36 and :43). This callee is spelled with an INLINE declarator and no typedef: `int (*cmp)(const void *a, const void *b, void *cmp_opaque)` at lib/librdkafka-2.15.0/src/rdkafka.h:1163-1166. The reader fails CLOSED, which is constraint 8 working; this is the first measurement of that boundary from production text. The withdrawal is LEAF-NEUTRAL - all 11 rows are same-position substitutions and no function's leaf count changed - which is why the module was kept rather than reverted: reverting it would delete the only evidence for this residual. Discharge condition: Extend the parameter declarator reader to the inline function-pointer form, on CONSTRUCTOR-RESIDUALS-ABI-TYPEDEF's own precedent. The projection it needs already exists (FUNCTION_POINTER_ABI_TYPE), so no new vocabulary is required.

named_followups.title: Two projected functions stay Unknown because their declaration is withdrawn, at zero leaf cost
named_followups.why: rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_sort_by_topic and rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_sort_by_topic_id (lib/librdkafka-2.15.0/src/rdkafka_partition.c:3675-3687) each hold exactly one leaf naming rd_kafka_topic_partition_list_sort. Card W37-CORPUS-CONTRACTS-4 declared that callee and the loader withdrew the declaration (see LOADER-ABI-INLINE-FNPTR-DECLARATOR), so both functions stayed Unknown against a prediction of Safe. The declaration itself was read line-cited and is faithful - all three formals borrowed, result none, permuting an array the caller owns whole changes no custody - so nothing about the reading is in doubt; only the reader's coverage is. named_followups.title: After wave 36's harvest the sole-blocker cover frontier is dominated by unit-internal `static` helpers, where declaration is structurally the wrong lever
named_followups.why: Card W37-CORPUS-CONTRACTS-4 (wave 37) re-derived the cover and surveyed 22 candidate callees for linkage, headers and definition counts. Ten are `static`/`static inline` DEFINED IN THE VERY UNIT THAT CALLS THEM (rd_kafka_topic_partition_destroy0, rd_kafka_destroy_app, sds_cat_safe, set_result, otlp_kvpair_list_destroy, destroy_context_list, crc32c_zeros, pack_kvlist, pack_context_metrics, rd_kafka_dump0) and three more have several definitions with DISAGREEING signatures. A resource contract is keyed by NAME, so for these a declaration is either meaningless (no extern C declaration for constraint 8's ABI gate to agree with) or wrong (it would speak for a neighbour's shape), and constraint 4's division of labour puts a body defined in its own calling unit on W4's side. This is why the card lands ten CUSTODY-NEUTRAL declarations and not one release - the exact inverse of W36's five releases plus one neutral - and the asymmetry is recorded in compiler/tests/contract_loader.rs's own pinned-table comment so it survives as a fact rather than as report rhetoric. Discharge condition: A W4-directed card attacking the same functions through summary derivation, or acceptance as a measured boundary on how far the declaration lever reaches in this corpus.

named_followups.title: A call nested in a modeled call's argument list is refused, and this is now the commonest way a decided leaf is exchanged rather than discharged
named_followups.why: Generalises CJSON-DELETE-NESTED-DETACH (wave 36) to a third library. Card W37-CORPUS-CONTRACTS-4 PREDICTED one instance ex ante and was exactly right: pack_string (lib/ctraces/src/ctr_encode_msgpack.c:35-38) is `mpack_write_str(writer, str, cfl_sds_len(str));`, and cfl_sds_len is a real external function (lib/cfl/src/cfl_sds.c:193, header lib/cfl/include/cfl/cfl_sds.h:69) that emits no leaf today only because the outer call refuses first. Once mpack_write_str was modeled the projection reached the inner call and refused there. The card also found two unlooked-for instances in cmt_encode_msgpack.c :: pack_metric (cmt_metric_hist_get_sum_value, cmt_metric_get_int64_value). Reading the target body ex ante converts W36-COVER-HIDDEN-BLOCKER from a surprise into a prediction, which is the method this residual recommends to any later cover card. Discharge condition: Admit the nested-call-in-argument-position shape in the resource projection, or declare/derive the inner callees. Note that declaring the inner callee alone does NOT help: the refusal is positional, not about the inner callee being uncontracted.

named_followups.title: Four ctraces formatters are blocked behind a `static` helper that becomes W4-derivable once two external callees are declared
named_followups.why: sds_cat_safe (lib/ctraces/src/ctr_encode_text.c:22) is `static inline`, has exactly one definition in the tree, and is defined in the unit that calls it, so card W37-CORPUS-CONTRACTS-4 declined to declare it (W37-COVER-FRONTIER-IS-STATIC). It blocks format_bool, format_double, format_int64 and format_string. Its own body calls only strlen and cfl_sds_cat_safe, both external and header-declared; W4 cannot derive a summary for it while those are uncontracted. The card's greedy cover measured that snprintf plus sds_cat_safe would free five functions where sole-blocker counting sees one, which is the set-yield effect a per-callee ranking misses. Discharge condition: Declare strlen and cfl_sds_cat_safe (and, for three of the four, snprintf - see LIBC-PRINTF-FAMILY), then re-measure whether W4 derives sds_cat_safe and the four formatters move.

named_followups.title: snprintf/sprintf/fprintf/vsnprintf are faithful in v1 today and carry ~3,200 leaves at near-zero function-cover yield: a LEAF-directed card, not a cover card
named_followups.why: Card W37-CORPUS-CONTRACTS-4 read them and declined them deliberately, on blast radius rather than faithfulness. There is NO vocabulary gap, and the reason is the exact inverse of LIBC-MEM-RESULT-ALIAS: their result is `int`, a SCALAR, so resource_return_none() is literally faithful rather than a conservative approximation; their buffer parameter is written through, which msgpack_packer_init's `pk` already establishes as borrowed; and their variadic tail is mk_print's resource_variadic_data_tail(). snprintf alone carries 1,044 leaves against a function-cover yield of ONE (rd_kafka_mk_nodename, itself forecast to exchange - its tail passes a `const char *` formal, the shape MK-PRINT-TAIL-ACTUALS measured refusing at 26 sites); sprintf's single target cJSON_Version returns a `static` local array, an independent exchange risk. Deciding 1,044 leaves inside a cover arbiter whose other declarations must each be attributable leaf by leaf would have made that card's movement unreadable, for one function. Discharge condition: A dedicated leaf-directed card landing the family together with its own leaf-by-leaf attribution, rather than smuggling one member into a cover card.

named_followups.title: A callee that releases its parameter only when a second, literal argument is nonzero cannot be declared in v1 without conditioning on that literal
named_followups.why: rd_kafka_topic_partition_destroy0 (lib/librdkafka-2.15.0/src/rdkafka_partition.c:2969-2982) ends `if (do_free) rd_free(rktpar);`. Its two target call sites (:3105, :3109) pass 1/rd_true, but five further sites in the same unit (:3098, :3122, :3600) pass 0. A contract is per-NAME and not per-site, so declaring `released` would be FALSE at those five sites and would move in the admitting direction, which invariant 1 forbids. Card W37-CORPUS-CONTRACTS-4 therefore declined it - also, independently, because it is `static` with no header declaration inside its own calling unit (W37-COVER-FRONTIER-IS-STATIC). The corpus does carry a `resource_literal_argument(PARAMETER, LITERAL)` clause that could in principle condition a contract on `do_free == 1`, which is why this is recorded as an avenue rather than as an impossibility. Discharge condition: A literal-conditioned release contract exercised on a real callee, or acceptance that W4 is the lever for unit-internal statics and this shape needs no declaration vocabulary.

named_followups.title: lib/cprofiles/*.c duplicates lib/cprofiles/src/*.c and the two copies are NOT identical
named_followups.why: Found incidentally by card W37-CORPUS-CONTRACTS-4's definition-count survey: lib/cprofiles/cprof_encode_opentelemetry.c and lib/cprofiles/src/cprof_encode_opentelemetry.c are both present and differ in size (92,051 vs 82,980 bytes), and the same stray-duplicate pattern applies to the whole lib/cprofiles/*.c set. Nothing in that card depends on it and no claim is made about which tree the pinned build compiles. It is recorded because a resource contract is keyed by NAME, so a future declaration naming anything defined in that library would meet two candidate definitions that disagree - the ADD-NAME-COLLISION hazard, latent. Discharge condition: Determine which of the two trees the pinned compile database actually builds, and record it beside the corpus conventions.

named_followups.title: A growable mpack writer's flush callback reallocates writer->buffer, so interior addresses are unstable across the declared calls
named_followups.why: Recorded by card W37-CORPUS-CONTRACTS-4 in contract/qcore/mpack/writer.qcore's own NOT CLAIMED list rather than hidden. Under mpack_writer_init_growable the flush callback reallocs writer->buffer, so a byte address inside the writer is not stable across mpack_write_cstr/str/i64/double. That is a fact about a FIELD of the borrowed object, not about the parameter's custody: the caller holds the mpack_writer_t *, that pointer is unchanged, and the caller's mpack_writer_destroy obligation is unchanged, which is all the declaration states. The v1 projection models parameter custody and has no interior-address vocabulary at all. Discharge condition: Acceptance as a stated boundary of the v1 projection, or an interior-address model - none exists today and none is proposed here.

named_followups.title: No emitted-program mutation was found that the unforced ThreadSanitizer harness misses and a forced schedule catches
named_followups.why: MEASURED by card TSAN-ROWS-2 (wave 39), docs/reports/tsan-rows-2/artifacts/catch-rates.json: the overlap mutation (both workers' byte writes rebased onto one byte) on CT07's case and on the flagship, and the join-edge-removal mutation on shared_readers and on CT07's case, are each reported in 20 of 20 runs under the unforced schedule AND under both forced schedules. The brief anticipated a mutation the unforced harness would miss at least once; none of these is it, and the reason is the one wave 37 stated - ThreadSanitizer detects a missing happens-before edge, not an observed interleaving, so two unordered accesses that both execute are reported whatever order the forcing puts them in. What the forced schedules measurably change is the REPORT SET, not the verdict: under halt_on_error=0 the shared_readers join-edge mutation yields 16 race reports unforced and 6 under either forced schedule. What they add is executed-schedule coverage: each forced row means 'this schedule, forced', with the realised schedule read back from the harness trace. The two asymmetries the card DID find run the other way and are registered separately (TSAN-FORCED-HARNESS-SYNC-INVISIBILITY, TSAN-FORCED-GATE-OPENED-BY-THE-JOIN). DISCHARGE: exhibit an emitted-program mutation the unforced harness provably misses - the candidate class is TSan's bounded shadow history (four cells per eight-byte word), which none of this route's programs can exhaust on the payload word - or state permanently that forcing adds coverage and not detection power.

named_followups.title: The together schedule forces creation, release and liveness, not the physical overlap of the two stores
named_followups.why: Card TSAN-ROWS-2 (wave 39). Under Schedule::ForcedTogether every worker of a cohort is created and released before any body runs and every thread of it stays live until every body has returned (an exit barrier), asserted on the harness's own stderr trace: all starts precede all leaves. What that does NOT force is that the two workers' store instructions overlap in time: nothing outside an emitted body can place a rendezvous inside it, and the harness changes no emitted byte by design. ThreadSanitizer's verdict does not depend on the overlap (it reasons about happens-before), so the clean rows' meaning is unaffected; what is unaffected too is CT07-TWO-THREAD-REPLAY-ORDER's observation that no evidence witnesses the two writes overlapping in time, which this card retires on its second arm (the TSan row is landed) while restating this boundary in its place. DISCHARGE: state permanently (the honest default), or an in-body rendezvous reachable through a runtime hook the emitter already carries - there is none at qcore_buffer_byte_write today, and adding one is an emission change with its own card.

named_followups.title: A forced schedule realised with synchronization ThreadSanitizer can see hides worker-versus-worker races; the shipped header is uninstrumented for that reason
named_followups.why: MEASURED by card TSAN-ROWS-2 (wave 39), and it is the card's finding. The first version of the forcing header (artifacts/schedule_forcing.v1-pthread.h) parked and released workers on a pthread mutex and condition variable; under the reverse policy the overlap mutation on CT07's case went UNREPORTED (artifacts/catch-point-reverse-mutex-edge.log) while the unforced and together schedules reported it: worker 2's byte write preceded its unlock, worker 1 woke by acquiring the same mutex, and TSan saw a release/acquire edge between the two writes. The shipped SCHEDULE_FORCING compiles every harness function with no_sanitize("thread"), keeps its bookkeeping behind an uninstrumented spinlock and parks a worker on a relaxed flag with sched_yield, so the only edges TSan observes are the program's own create and join; the reverse row then reports the overlap 20 of 20. The reproduction is shipped as mutate.sh's hook_visible_to_tsan (re-instrument the header and take the spinlock once before a body: the reverse arm goes red by MISSING the race). This is a rule about any future forcing harness, stated here so it is indexed. DISCHARGE: keep the header uninstrumented and the reproduction mutation red whenever the header changes; a header that must synchronize visibly needs a row showing each forced schedule still reports the overlap mutation.

named_followups.title: That the transport model's cross-name coupling IS the shared logical state of a connection is measured, not proved
named_followups.why: Card CT42-CELL-ROUTE (wave 39) routes the derived protocol cell from source and audits the DERIVATION (QCore.SocketFootprint: an accepted pair shares one cell, a fresh cell is no existing cell, the three unpaired arms refuse, an admitted accept takes an existing cell) and the T09 narrowing (QCore.SocketCellRoute). What no theorem states is the ground the cell rests on: that in qcore_core::std_socket's transport model an operation through one end of a completed connection is decided by state the other end established (a send's in-flight bound read off the peer's stream; a close refused while the peer's bytes sit unread; a send refused when the peer is closed). Those are the Rust checker's measured rules, documented in socket_footprint.rs and observed by the route's tests, and QCore.StdSocket carries no theorem about peer coupling. So the sentence `the two ends of one connection share one protocol cell` is proved as a fact about the derivation and observed as a fact about the transport model. DISCHARGE: a QCore.StdSocket theorem that a connected pair's admissible operations are mutually dependent (a send's admission depends on the peer's state, a close's on the peer's committed bytes), cited from the socket_footprint module doc in place of the measured sentence.

named_followups.title: CT42's three accepted controls emit C that no runner compiles or executes

The route's native evidence is the published examples' (tcp_echo, udp_echo), not these programs'. The question erases from emission, so what an accepted control would add natively is a run of a program that spells one; nothing is claimed for it. DISCHARGE: a named workspace test that compiles and runs listener_question.qcore's emitted C under ASan/UBSan and compares its streams with the route's observation, or a sequential-reject control runner on the CT34-SANITIZED precedent, crediting the control's own file and never the case's.

named_followups.title: A lend or a borrow opened inside a for body is a per-iteration loan, refused by name on both routes
named_followups.why: Card LOOPS-ON-COMPOSED-ROUTES (wave 39) computes a loan's window over iterations for a TOP-LEVEL loan: a loan a loop body names is live across the whole loop, proved sound relative to LOOP-V1's unrolling (QCore.LoopWindows). A loan OPENED inside a body is a different construct - its window opens and closes inside one iteration and is not an interval of top-level statement indices at all, so neither the theorem nor the lend-structured projection (whose borrow nodes are top-level windows) covers it. It is refused by name: a `lend(...)` inside a body at Q051 on the buffer route and at Q077 on the composed route (checker, before the window function runs), and a `borrow_utf8(...)` inside a body at Q077 at the composed lowering. Mutation M3 shows the buffer-route refusal load-bearing: without it the per-iteration lend's stores reach the inherited checker as no operation and the program is ADMITTED. DISCHARGE: a per-iteration window - a borrow node opened and closed inside the unrolled body at every iteration - with its own exclusivity statement against the top-level loans live across the loop, landed in the IR rather than in a route (constraint 15h), or the shape recorded as a permanent measured boundary.

named_followups.title: A for body neither acquires nor releases where a loan is held: refused by name on the lending buffer route and on the composed route
named_followups.why: Card LOOPS-ON-COMPOSED-ROUTES (wave 39). On the plain buffer route (no lend) a loop body may acquire and release, decided by LOOP-V1's per-iteration identity gate (Q099) over the unrolled operation list with per-iteration scoped names. In an entry that LENDS the projection is the lend-structured one, which opens borrow nodes over top-level windows and produces no identity gates, and on the composed string route the custody list is a flat unrolling with no gates either - so a custody step inside an iteration would be decided by neither gate. Rather than admit it, an acquisition or a release inside a body is refused by name at Q051 (buffer route, entries that lend) and Q077 (composed route). The refusal is fail-closed and the direct-caller path cannot admit: a body release the projection never saw leaves the owner live at the normal exit (the inherited leak), a body acquisition it never saw makes every later use an unknown name. DISCHARGE: produce LOOP-V1's identity gates on both projections (the prefix inside a borrow node's body being the open question) and lift the refusal with a test per shape, or record it as a permanent measured boundary.

named_followups.title: A for body on the composed string route is source.buffer.v1's vocabulary; a string construct, a text line, a len-bound header or an unrolling licence inside one is refused
named_followups.why: Card LOOPS-ON-COMPOSED-ROUTES (wave 39) lowers a `for` in a composed module through source.buffer.v1's own loop reader, so the body is that route's statement grammar: a string view, `len`, `concat` or a text line (`print "..."`) inside a body is refused at Q077 by name at the lowering; a loop bound naming a `len(s)` binding is refused by the loop's own Q098 (the lowering-visible tier holds literal lets and extents, not view lengths); and a `[| #unroll, where #bound < N |]` clause list before a composed `for` refuses at Q068 as a statement the string route does not model, so a composed loop is held to the default budget. Each is fail-closed and measured (loops_on_composed_routes.rs section 5). DISCHARGE: extend the composed route's body grammar construct by construct, each with the window consequence stated (a view read inside a body lengthens the window through view_uses_at_any_depth, already written for it), or record the boundary as permanent.

named_followups.title: A mutation harness that restores a source file by mv from a cp backup leaves the file older than the mutant's build, and cargo keeps the mutated rlib
named_followups.why: Proposed, not registered, by card LOOPS-ON-COMPOSED-ROUTES (wave 39) section 12 item 8 and section 6, and registered by the wave-39 close. The mechanism is the second route to the hazard MUTATION-HARNESS-MTIME-RESTORE (wave 35) recorded for shutil.copy2: `mv` of a `cp` backup (and `cp -p`) keeps the backup's mtime, which predates the build cargo made from the mutant, so cargo's fingerprint reads the restored file as unchanged and every later run links the mutated crate while git status reads clean. That card's first full gate ran against exactly that: exit 101 with three red rows of its own test file (docs/reports/loops-on-composed-routes/gate/run1/), repaired by one `touch` after each restore plus a green baseline before and after (its mutations.sh). MEASURED by the wave-39 close over every shipped harness in docs/reports/ (seventeen files, `find docs/reports -name 'mutat*'`): twelve restore by rewriting (write_text/write_bytes - aggregate-owned-field, c-gateway-constant-do-while, c-gateway-return-call-w4, ct07-two-thread-proof-leg and stability-reeval-3 (both also os.utime into the future), ct42-cell-route, joined-provenance-call-frames, joined-provenance-cycles, mutex-share-cross-arms, scalar-route-exit-edge, wave36-close, wave38-close); four by `cp` from a backup, which writes a fresh mtime (c-gateway-return-position without a touch; task-route-tsan's mutate.sh and mutate2.sh and tsan-rows-2's mutate.sh each with a touch); one by `mv` plus `touch` (loops-on-composed-routes, the hazard's own, repaired). None is mtime-preserving today, and the CLAUDE.md rule now names the mv/cp -p mechanism beside copy2. DISCHARGE: the survey made mechanical - a script under scripts/ that lists every shipped harness's restore mechanism and exits nonzero on an mtime-preserving one (mv of a backup without a touch, copy2, cp -p), with a test red by mutation, run at each close; until then a close re-runs the hand survey and records it.

named_followups.title: An integration gate's clang presence claim is checked against the card's recording beside it, not against a recording of the integration run

named_followups.title: A --check verify claim may quote a mutable pointer, so a frozen close's record goes permanently red on an ordinary later action

So the record is now permanently red through no fault of the close, and the next wave-opening commit was CERTAIN to happen when the claim was written. The content --check itself is sound and non-vacuous: _verify_claim (:728-766) opens the named file, rejects path escapes (:748-751) and tests a whitespace-normalised substring (:758), and coverage is 100% in both waves (wave 38, 6 of 6 applied items carry a non-empty verify; wave 39, 31 of 31), with the unverifiable escape hatch (:797-816) unused. DISCHARGE: a recorded rule that a verify claim quotes DURABLE text (never a current-file pointer, a count or a date), OR a --check mode that distinguishes 'applied and later legitimately superseded' from 'never applied', with the wave-39 claim reclassified under whichever lands. DECIDED AND STILL OPEN at the wave-40 close, with the class measured far wider than this entry states. Re-running the wave-39 close's own command at 0c7b0cea fails 16 of its 57 verify claims, not one. Attributed commit by commit by testing each claim's normalised needle against `git show <rev>:<path>` at 6dc484ad, f11ccbba, d6a57f66 and 0c7b0cea: ONE (the increments-index pointer this entry names) broke at the wave-opening commit f11ccbba, and FIFTEEN broke at the DOCS-COMPACT-8 merge 0c7b0cea - fourteen in AGENTS.md, one in CLAUDE.md - none at the reeval merge. DURABILITY IS A PROPERTY OF THE TARGET FILE: every claim into the acceptance matrix (17), a frozen increment record (4), the spec (3), crate source (2), the CT manifest and its fixture (2) and a frozen card report (1) survived; 15 of the 27 into AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md did not. So the FIRST discharge arm - 'quote durable text' - is INSUFFICIENT ON ITS OWN, measured: verifying an AGENTS.md amendment in AGENTS.md is the point of the arm, and a compaction card is chartered to rewrite exactly that prose. The close recorded the operative rule in CLAUDE.md (a --check is green at its own close and only there; a later red is evidence of supersession, not of a defect, and is never repaired by editing a frozen record; prefer the most durable location an amendment genuinely allows). DISCHARGE IS NOW THE SECOND ARM ALONE: a --check mode distinguishing 'applied and later legitimately superseded' from 'never applied' - for instance a claim pinned to the commit it was verified at, or a per-close snapshot the check reads - with the wave-39 record's 16 claims reclassified under it.

named_followups.title: CT50's proof row covers the capability half of its scenario; the numeric address reuse the scenario is named after is native observation only
named_followups.why: Registered by card CT-PROOF-LEG-3 (wave 41) with the row it created, so the row cannot be over-read. CT50's scenario is 'New lifetime reuses old numeric address/descriptor' and its native evidence places the second mapping at the first one's address with MAP_FIXED_NOREPLACE (run_native_task_scenarios, the pinned stderr transcript MAP 1 / UNMAP 1 / MAP 2 / REUSED_ADDRESS / UNMAP 2 / RUN_CLEAN 2). The F02 observation alphabet carries GENERATIONS and not addresses, so the reuse is invisible to it: QCore.Ct50LifetimeIdentity proves that the two generation lifetimes are disjoint, that no fact of the run uses the old generation, and that the one read names the new generation with the new allocation's own payload -- all of which would hold equally if the second mapping landed somewhere else. The address-level fact is therefore observed and not proved, in exactly constraint 15n's 'separate the proved side from the observed side' sense. DISCHARGE: either an alphabet that carries a mapping identity beside the generation (an extension on CT03-PROOF-ALPHABET's method, with the same conservativity obligation), or an explicit decision that address identity stays native evidence, recorded in the manifest's CT50 semantic profile rather than only here. Until then the row reads: the scenario property proved of the checked artifact's reference run and its admitted renderings, address reuse covered by observation only.

named_followups.title: The new digest cross-check compares two source texts, not a value the Lean kernel handed it
named_followups.why: Registered by card CT-PROOF-LEG-3 (wave 41) with the mechanism it built, discharging PROOF-LEG-DIGESTS-UNCROSSCHECKED but not more than it. compiler/tests/proof_leg_digests.rs reads the numeral out of each 'theorem ct<N>...digest : ... = <numeral> :=' line in proof/QCore/ and compares it with the corresponding compiler/tests/ constant. That closes the re-transcription hole it was built for -- a digit changed on either side goes red, measured as D1, D2 and D3, and a Lean theorem deleted goes red as D4 -- and it rests on one premise it does not itself check: that the numeral in the .lean SOURCE is the numeral the kernel decided. The standing scripts/check_lean_audits.py gate is what makes that true (the theorem is 'by decide' and the audit builds it), so the premise is discharged by a DIFFERENT gate step rather than by this test, and a tree where the Lean build was skipped would pass this test on two agreeing but unchecked texts. The parser is also line-shaped: a digest theorem whose statement is split across lines, or written with a different numeral spelling, is not seen -- fail-open in that one direction, which is why CASES_WITH_A_DIGEST_PIN is pinned beside it as the fail-closed half. DISCHARGE: emit the digests from Lean itself (a #eval or a generated file the test reads) so the compared value comes from the kernel's own elaboration rather than from a line of source, or state this premise in the file and accept it deliberately.

named_followups.title: The documentation restructure's status snapshot asserts equality with the live tree, so the first card after it diverges by design
named_followups.why: MEASURED by card CT-PROOF-LEG-3 (wave 41), the first card to land after the restructure 96142e49. docs/reports/docs-structure-compression/rederive_status.py --check asserts that its status-sources.json still EQUALS what it re-derives from primary inputs (the manifest's proof and native_sanitized ids, the corpus artifacts, the contract corpus, named_followups carried and derived, the wave-40 gate.json, and the Audit*.lean count). NOTHING GOES RED: the script is invoked by no scripts/tests test, by check_lean_audits.py, or by any CI step in this repository, verified by grep at this tip; and its file is that card's own frozen checkpoint, which constraint 21 says to leave alone rather than refresh. So the divergence is the checkpoint behaving as a checkpoint, not a defect -- but it is undeclared: the script's docstring says it checks 'this card's checkpoint, not all future rule revisions', while the --check arm's message ('status sources moved since this checkpoint') reads as a failure to whoever runs it next. DISCHARGE: either state in that report that --check is expected to diverge once any later card lands and is therefore a checkpoint re-derivation tool rather than a gate, or move the snapshot to a regenerated artifact with its own provenance record beside the frozen one (constraint 21's dual-publication shape). named_followups.title: AggregateAtOwnerPosition and NotAnAggregate remain unreachable from any source program, and are kept as the IR's fail-closed backstop
named_followups.why: Successor to OWNED-FIELD-IR-REFUSALS-UNREACHED, which OWNED-FIELD-ROUTE-REACH (wave 41) retired by the documentation arm of its own discharge. The measurement survives the retirement and is recorded here so it does not disappear: the two IR refusals are UNREACHABLE FROM ANY SOURCE PROGRAM. Verified by this card through the real pipeline (docs/reports/owned-field-route-reach/scripts/reach.py, probes ir-aggregate-at-owner-lend, ir-aggregate-at-owner-index, ir-not-an-aggregate): a lend of a record refuses at Q051 naming OWNED-FIELD-LEND-WINDOW, a byte access on one at Q052 ('read the field you mean first'), and a field path on a plain buffer at Q052 ('is not a record this entry constructed') - the route's own gates deciding every shape that would build such an operation, and firing first BY DESIGN because each gives the better-localised message. This is a deliberate backstop rather than dead code: it fails closed for any future route that reaches the IR without such a gate. DISCHARGE: either a source fixture on some route that reaches either refusal through the real pipeline with the message pinned - the two candidates are named, AGGREGATE-ROUTE-WIDENING (a record admitted on the sequential route, where whole_program builds operations from names with no kind gate) and OWNED-FIELD-LEND-WINDOW's discharge (the lend projection generalised to field paths) - or a decision to delete the variants once no route can present the shape at all, which would be a weakening and needs invariant 1 argued.

named_followups.title: The copy bind and source.socket.v1's creation form are the same token shape, separated by route selection alone
named_followups.why: MEASURED by OWNED-FIELD-ROUTE-REACH (wave 41) in its constraint-14 census (docs/reports/owned-field-route-reach/scripts/census.py, 535 .qcore/.qc files): `let NAME = NAME;` occurs 29 times in the tree and EVERY occurrence is source.socket.v1's `let listener = tcp;` / `let client = udp;` in the socket, HTTP, event and CT42 families. The card therefore did not add the shape to source_std_buffer::buffer_use - the function that decides route selection and that the composed string/buffer route reads this route's statements through - so the two constructs are separated by route selection and by nothing else. That separation is currently pinned by two tests (the_socket_routes_creation_form_is_untouched, the_composed_string_route_keeps_its_own_refusal) and by the examples suite, but it is a property of the DISPATCH ORDER rather than of either grammar: a future route-selection change could move 29 published programs between routes without either reader changing. DISCHARGE: either a structural guard that makes the collision impossible to resolve wrongly (the two shapes told apart by a token rather than by which route was selected), or a route-selection test that enumerates every program of the claimed shape in the tree and asserts its profile, so the 29 are checked rather than sampled.

named_followups.title: An admitted source.buffer.v1 program whose let binding is never read emits C that -Wall -Wextra -Werror refuses
named_followups.why: MEASURED in passing by OWNED-FIELD-ROUTE-REACH (wave 41), and INHERITED rather than introduced: `let n = 5;` with no later use is admitted by the route and emits `int32_t s_n = INT32_C(5);`, which clang 21.1.8 refuses under the examples suite's own flags with -Werror,-Wunused-variable (measured: quirin emit exit 0, cc exit 1). The copy bind this card lands inherits the property exactly - an unused copy is an unused binding - and so do the acquisition, the extent read and the byte read. It is fail-closed (a failure, not a silent miscompilation) and no shipped program is affected, because every published program uses what it binds; the composed string/buffer route already solves it by emitting an explicit (void) discard for an unconsumed binding (std_string_c_emit::buffer_consumers). DISCHARGE: either the same discard scan on the plain buffer route, or a route-level refusal of an unused binding with its own condition stated in section L21 - the second being the fail-closed direction and the one that tells the author rather than the C compiler.

named_followups.title: A loop bound or a lend footprint spelled through a copy bind is refused rather than followed, because the lowering's constant tier is deliberately narrower than the checker's
named_followups.why: Landed by OWNED-FIELD-ROUTE-REACH (wave 41) as a deliberate non-widening, the LOOP-BOUND-FROM-BYTE and WRITE-LEND-BOUND-FROM-BYTE shape. LoweringConstants::observe gives the copy bind an explicit do-nothing arm: the lowering's tier is an integer literal, a literal `let` and an `extent` binding, and following a copy there would decide a loop bound and a lend footprint in a second place. Measured through the real pipeline: `let n = 2; let m = n; for i in 0..m` refuses at Q098 and `lend(b, 0, m)` at Q053 (a_bound_spelled_through_a_copy_is_refused_rather_than_followed). The CHECKER's tier does follow the copy - both the flat and the lend-structured custody projections carry a copied scalar's value forward, so an INDEX written through a copy resolves - which is why the two tiers are named separately here. DISCHARGE: a card that widens the lowering tier once (for the byte read, the field read and the copy together, with the bound decided in one place), or a decision that the tier stays literal-only, recorded with the three refusals as its consequence.

named_followups.title: The copy bind is admitted on source.buffer.v1 alone; every other route's refusal is measured and pinned rather than widened
named_followups.why: Recorded by OWNED-FIELD-ROUTE-REACH (wave 41) as the boundary of its own admission, the LOOP-ROUTE-WIDENING shape. `let NAME = NAME;` is read by source_std_buffer::lower_let and by nothing else: it is deliberately NOT a buffer_use, so the composed string/buffer route never lowers one and `let t = s;` there keeps the Q068 it always had (measured, the_composed_string_route_keeps_its_own_refusal), and the sequential, standard-IO, extern, socket, event, HTTP and task routes keep their own refusals untouched. The consequence worth naming: the ownership IR's copy rule is now reached by ONE route, so 'no program can copy an owner' is a statement about source.buffer.v1 and not about the language. DISCHARGE: either the copy bind lowered on the sequential route (which would also be OWNED-FIELD-SEQUENTIAL-UNREACHED's first arm, since whole_program would then build a Copy reaching Q103), or a recorded decision that the other routes' value binds are each that route's own construct, with the per-route refusal measured as this card measured the composed string route's.

named_followups.title: The migration's residual-discovery check fails when a candidate becomes a card or is cited in the tracker, which is not a loss
named_followups.why: Measured by the integrator at the wave-41 merges. docs/reports/docs-structure-compression/check_residuals.py compares the untracked-residual CANDIDATE set produced by the pre-restructure sweep over the 463fa6e8 files with the set the current sweep produces over the live tree, and asserts the difference is empty. Two ordinary mechanisms remove a name from the candidate set without any discoverability being lost: (1) the name acquires docs/reports/<card>/README.md and is classified a CARD NAME rather than a residual - CT-PROOF-LEG-3, whose own card landed in wave 41; (2) the name is cited inside a tracker entry's `why`, so --residuals no longer reports it as untracked - CT03-PROOF-ALPHABET, newly cited by CT-PROOF-F02-CANDIDATES-EXHAUSTED and CT50-PROOF-ADDRESS-REUSE-UNPROVED; that mechanism is registered as RESIDUAL-QUIET-BY-PROSE-MENTION by the wave-40 close. Measured: the check exits 0 at 96142e49 and fails at the CT-PROOF-LEG-3 merge naming exactly those two. The script is a frozen card's own evidence (constraint 21) and is in no scripts/tests test and no CI step, so nothing goes red in the standing gate; what is at risk is the check's usefulness, since as written it will fail on every wave that lands a card report or cites a name in the tracker. DISCHARGE: a card that re-expresses the lost arm over CLASSES rather than raw candidate sets - a name may leave the candidate set by becoming a card name, by being registered, or by being cited in tracker text, and only a name that leaves for none of those reasons is a loss - published beside the frozen script rather than by editing it; or a recorded decision that the check is a one-shot migration artifact that later waves do not run.

named_followups.title: A bare `print s;` of a view inside a composed for body is kept out by a rendering rule, not by a window rule
named_followups.why: MEASURED by card COMPOSED-WINDOW-REACH (wave 41). The composed string route's window function contributes nothing at a `for` (std_string::view_uses_at_any_depth's depth half is empty for every input, pinned by the_depth_contribution_is_empty_for_every_event), so its soundness rests entirely on no admitted composed body being able to read a view. That rests on THREE mechanisms, not the one the code claimed. (1) a body holds BufferEvents and no BufferEvent constructor names a view - a type-level fact. (2) a body statement that CONSTRUCTS a view (a quoted literal, a len, a concat, an inline-slice render, a borrow_utf8) is refused at Q077 by name (LOOP-ON-COMPOSED-ROUTE-BODY-VOCABULARY / LOOP-PER-ITERATION-LOAN), measured over six spellings. (3) a BARE name at a rendering operand - `print s;`, `log info s;` - is DELIBERATELY NOT claimed by StringUse::Render (source_std_string.rs:270-284: a bare name must not pull a module that never mentions a string onto this route, so `print bogus;` keeps refusing at Q030). It is refused instead by source.buffer.v1's own line reader, whose message is '`print` names a `std.fmt` rendering: `dec` or `hex`' - measured, probes/verdicts.log rows P1/P1b/P1c/P4. That third mechanism is a RENDERING rule doing a window's work. It is incidental: a card that admitted a selector-free `print NAME;` on the buffer route, or that gave the buffer route a view-shaped scalar, would remove it without reading constraint 15h. Pinned by a_bare_render_of_a_view_inside_a_composed_body_is_refused, which asserts BOTH that the message is the rendering one and that it is NOT the vocabulary one, so making the closure deliberate turns the row red rather than passing silently. NOT A DEFECT TODAY: no program is wrongly admitted (21 probes, section 2 of the report). DISCHARGE: claim the bare-name render at a composed `for` body in body_string_use so mechanism 3 becomes a window rule with its own name and message, and rewrite this test's second assertion; OR make the window's depth recursion live by admitting a view read in a composed body, which retires the question; OR record the incidental closure as a permanent measured boundary in constraint 15h, which already names it.

named_followups.title: The window function refuses a field path rather than giving it a window, and the card that lifts the owned-field refusals must do the latter
named_followups.why: Card COMPOSED-WINDOW-REACH (wave 41) discharged WINDOW-FIELD-ARM-UNREACHED on the second of its two disjuncts - 'the arms must be made an explicit refusal rather than an empty vector' - and this is what that choice leaves open. std_buffer::custody_names_at_any_depth now classifies names as WindowName::Binding or WindowName::FieldPath, and window_unnameable_events turns a field path into a refusal by name at Q051 (a condition extension; no code allocated), reached from lend_windows. So the day OWNED-FIELD-LEND-WINDOW or OWNED-FIELD-LOOP-BODY is lifted, the window function REFUSES rather than silently forgetting - fail-closed, the direction invariant 1 wants - but it still does not WINDOW a field path. What is missing is the key space: a lend binding is one identifier, and a window keyed by `RECORD.FIELD` needs the map, the LendWindow binding field, the custody projection's segment walk (which addresses owners by plain name, OWNED-FIELD-LEND-WINDOW's own stated ground) and crossed_lend_windows to agree about paths. Measured beside it: the gate is unreachable from source today - a 535-program emission census moved no verdict in either direction - so this is a tripwire and not a live refusal. DISCHARGE: the card that lifts either owned-field refusal must, in the same change, give the four Field* arms real windows (a key space that holds a path, through the projection and crossed_lend_windows), land a test that shows the window LENGTHENING across a field-path use in a body, and retire this gate deliberately; OR record the refusal as permanent, which means an entry that lends never composes an owned field.

named_followups.title: The Lean-to-Rust window binding is eight shared vectors, not an extraction, and says nothing about a ninth program
named_followups.why: Card COMPOSED-WINDOW-REACH (wave 41) discharged LOOPWINDOWS-LEAN-IS-A-TRANSCRIPTION on two of its three disjuncts: the unrolling is instantiated at a lend-carrying alphabet (QCore.LoopWindows.LendEvent, the_lend_alphabets_unrolling_is_loop_v1s_recursion beside loop_v1s_unrolling_is_the_same_flattening), and the doc-comment link is replaced by a differential test over shared vectors - compiler/tests/composed_window_reach.rs reads proof/QCore/LoopWindows.lean AS TEXT, extracts all eight rows of its `agreement` table, rebuilds each spelling as a Vec<BufferEvent> and asserts last_uses returns the Lean number, while the Lean side proves the_agreement_table_holds (each row's spelling is its own program's rendering AND each row's number is lastUse's answer). Non-vacuity is measured in both directions: W41-M6 moves one row's number in the LEAN file and the Rust test goes red; W41-M7 moves one row's SPELLING and the Lean build fails. WHAT IS NOT PROVED: that last_uses and lastUse agree on any program OUTSIDE those eight. The binding is finite by construction - eight vectors chosen to exercise a flat last use, a body-only use, a nested-body use, a loop naming another binding, a use before and inside a loop, and a program with no use - and a divergence on a ninth shape would be invisible to it. The Rust test guards the table's size (>= 8 rows) and pins the body-only row, so shrinking the vector set is a red row rather than a silent loss. PROVED: properties of the Lean model, at an alphabet the implementation produces. OBSERVED, on eight points: that the Rust function is that model. DISCHARGE: an extraction, a generated digest over the two definitions, or a property-based/exhaustive differential over generated programs up to a stated depth and alphabet - any of which replaces 'eight points' with a quantifier; OR this sentence carried as the binding's stated boundary.

named_followups.title: The cohort release trigger costs catches on the join-edge-removal mutation, so it is an addition to the join trigger and not a replacement
named_followups.why: MEASURED by card TSAN-FAILURE-ARMS (wave 41), docs/reports/tsan-failure-arms/artifacts/catch-rates.json. The new QCORE_FORCED_COHORT trigger opens the forcing gate inside the create hook, before the creator reaches any join, which is what catches the gate-closed mutation TSAN-FORCED-GATE-OPENED-BY-THE-JOIN recorded (0 of 20 at cohort 0, 20 of 20 at cohort 2 under both forced schedules). It also COSTS catches elsewhere: at cohort 2 the join-edge-removal mutation is reported 0 of 20 on shared_readers AND on CT07's case under forced-together, and 18 of 20 on shared_readers under forced-reverse, against 20 of 20 at wave 39's join-only trigger. The workers are released at creation, run and finish long before the creator's post-join access, and what ThreadSanitizer reports becomes a thread leak rather than a data race. The card's response is to keep BOTH triggers - the two committed wave-39 mutation rows stay at cohort 0, the clean rows run at the row's own cohort, and both cohorts are measured in the published table - rather than to weaken either row. DISCHARGE: a release trigger that fires before the join AND leaves the creator's post-join access unordered relative to worker bodies ThreadSanitizer still holds shadow history for; or state permanently, keeping both triggers measured and the two wave-39 rows at cohort 0.

named_followups.title: The NULL-allocator failure arm creates no thread, so its clean ThreadSanitizer verdict is about a single-threaded recovery path
named_followups.why: Card TSAN-FAILURE-ARMS (wave 41) landed TSan rows over both failure arms TSAN-FORCED-SCHEDULE-FAILURE-ARMS named. The refusing-QCORE_TASK_CREATE arm IS thread-live: the first worker is created, released, runs its body and is joined inside the arm. The NULL-returning-QCORE_BUFFER_MALLOC arm is NOT: on both subjects (the write-lend flagship and CT07's case.qcore) the only allocation is the entry's own qcore_buffer_new(0)?, which stands BEFORE any spawn, so the error edge is taken with no thread in existence and TSan has no second thread to reason about. The row is real - the arm executes, under TSan, clean, with its stdout byte-identical to the reference run scripted for the same outcome, 20 of 20 under each of the three schedules - and it is weak, and this says so rather than letting the cell count read as thread evidence. WHAT WOULD REACH IT: an admitted program on this route that acquires a buffer AFTER a spawn; none is spelled today, and the nearest existing shape is CT16's worker_allocation.h fixture, which is not a TSan subject. DISCHARGE: a TSan row over an allocation failure occurring while a worker is live; or state permanently that this route's allocation-failure arm is single-threaded by construction.

named_followups.title: The forcing harness's per-program cohort count is read off each program's text by the row's author, not derived from the checked artifact
named_followups.why: Card TSAN-FAILURE-ARMS (wave 41). QCORE_FORCED_COHORT is 'the number of workers this program parks in one cohort', and every row supplies it as a literal: SUBJECTS' third column in compiler/tests/task_route_tsan.rs, and the per-arm counts in failure_arms() (1 for the spawn-refusal arm, which creates one worker; 0 for the allocation-failure arm, which creates none). Nothing derives it from the checked task IR, so a subject whose source changes its spawn count silently gets a wrong cohort. The consequence is bounded but real: a too-large cohort never fires and the row falls back to the join trigger (wave 39's behaviour, still correct but no longer testing what the row says), and a too-small one releases early, which the schedule-shape assertion usually but not always catches - mutation rows_cohort_is_the_row_s shows it catching exactly that. DISCHARGE: derive the count from the checked task IR (the TrySpawn spans preceding the first Join, the ordering REGION-CREDIT-JOINS' Q600 condition already reads) and assert each row's literal against it; or state permanently, with the schedule-shape assertion named as the guard.

named_followups.title: removing_the_join_edge_is_reported_under_every_schedule misses its ct07-case forced-together cell under concurrent whole-workspace load, and passes it 20 of 20 in isolation
named_followups.why: MEASURED by card TSAN-FAILURE-ARMS (wave 41) at its rebased gate, and recorded in BOTH directions rather than absorbed. Inside `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` with three sibling worktrees building concurrently, removing_the_join_edge_is_reported_under_every_schedule (compiler/tests/task_route_tsan.rs, wave 39's row, whose behaviour this card did not change - it runs at cohort 0, wave 39's own join trigger) failed at its ct07-case @ forced-together cell: ThreadSanitizer reported a THREAD LEAK instead of a data race, with the schedule trace showing both workers started and left (docs/reports/tsan-failure-arms/gate/red-row.log). ON THE SAME BINARY AND THE SAME TREE the whole file is 18 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored in isolation (gate/row-isolation.exit 0), and the row alone ran TWENTY times at load average 5.78 with 0 OF 20 RED (gate/row-isolation-20-runs.log). The card's own 20-run table had measured this cell at 20 of 20 on a quiet host (artifacts/catch-rates.json, 'join-edge-removed/ct07-case @ cohort 0 @ forced-together'), so this is a load observation and not a new defect, and the assertion is deliberately NOT weakened and the row is NOT ignored. The mechanism is the one TSAN-COHORT-TRIGGER-CATCH-COST names from the other side: what this mutation's detection depends on is that the creator's post-join access still has the workers' accesses in ThreadSanitizer's shadow history, and anything that lets the workers finish far earlier - a release trigger, or a loaded machine descheduling the creator - can cost the report. DISCHARGE: measure the row under controlled load to establish the rate (the P02-FLAKE method), then either add it to rule 16's enumerated load-sensitive rows - a decision above a card, since that rule lives in a preserved span - or make the row insensitive by asserting on ThreadSanitizer's report SET rather than on a data race specifically, which would weaken what it measures and needs its own argument.

named_followups.title: docs-structure-compression's status-sources.json is a frozen checkpoint that its own --check compares against live inputs, so the first legitimate tracker edit after it makes that check stale
named_followups.why: MEASURED by card TSAN-FAILURE-ARMS (wave 41), the first card to move a tracker count after the documentation restructure at 96142e49. docs/reports/docs-structure-compression/rederive_status.py --check re-derives the status snapshot from PRIMARY INPUTS (the CT manifest, the w37 corpus artifacts, contract/qcore, the wave-40 close's gate.json, proof/Audit*.lean and the acceptance matrix) and asserts it equals the archived status-sources.json. This card's tracker delta - three retirements and four registrations, named_followups 257 -> 258 - moves EXACTLY ONE field of that archive, followups {carried 257, derived 257} -> {258, 258}, and nothing else: lean_audits stays 141, contracts.modules stays 88, and the ct, corpus and last_merged_gate blocks are untouched (measured, not assumed). The archive is NOT edited, because it is a frozen checkpoint (constraint 21), and the script is NOT run by the standing gate - nothing in scripts/tests/, no Rust test and no CI step references it, so no gate row is red and this is a latent staleness rather than a failure. Its sibling verify.py is unaffected: it reconstructs the pre-restructure guides from git show <source_commit>:<source>, so it is checkpoint-scoped by construction and stays green. This is the D02-B00-LEDGER-SNAPSHOT shape - a derived figure reading a frozen archive beside a live source - and it is a decision above a card. DISCHARGE: publish provenance beside status-sources.json (the fields a later wave is expected to move, and where the live figure is read instead), or make the checkpoint re-derivable on demand with the archived copy labelled as the migration's own observation; never by editing the archive to match a later tree.

named_followups.title: The enforced invisibility property is a forbidden-primitive list plus one measured mutation, not a statement about every visible forcing design
named_followups.why: Card TSAN-FAILURE-ARMS (wave 41) discharged TSAN-HEADER-INVISIBILITY-UNENFORCED with two committed tests, and states here what they do not cover. Half one (the_forcing_header_stays_invisible_to_thread_sanitizer) is a LIST: the shipped header must carry no_sanitize("thread") on every static qcore_forced_ function and must not name any of pthread_mutex, pthread_cond, pthread_barrier, pthread_rwlock, sem_wait, mtx_lock, mtx_init, cnd_wait, cnd_signal, cnd_broadcast. A future design synchronising visibly through a primitive outside that list, or outside the qcore_forced_ namespace, passes it. Half two (a_visible_forcing_header_would_hide_the_overlap_which_is_why_the_shipped_one_is_not) measures ONE mutation - the pthread-mutex park-and-release shape wave 39 actually built - going 0 of 20 against the shipped header's 20 of 20; it is a witness that visible synchronization can hide a race, not a proof that every visible design does. DISCHARGE: a property-shaped check (for instance, that no symbol the header references is one ThreadSanitizer intercepts) or an argument that the namespace check is exhaustive; or state permanently as the measured boundary of the enforcement.

named_followups.title: The CT10 source profile proves footprint independence only on a successful spawn/join window
named_followups.why: The profile explicitly records SpawnAndJoinSucceed and does not execute the scoped-task custody ledger. A propagated second-spawn failure may leave an earlier child outstanding in source forms outside that property claim; admitting disjoint footprints is not a lifetime judgment. Discharge: compose the generic task ledger with the explicit-layout source profile, exercise failed creation/join recovery with live siblings, and provide matching audited Lean semantics before exporting a scoped-task certificate. Keep the current property-only certificate and CLI boundary until then.

named_followups.title: The bounded atomic-publication judgment CT41 maps on is reachable only from tests
named_followups.why: Re-measured on the landed tree (merge 2910c1e0), not inherited from the pre-merge measurement: `qcore_verification::atomic_publication_source::check_atomic_publication_source` is called from `crates/qcore-verification/tests/atomic_publication_source.rs` and from `compiler/tests/support/ct_atomic_publication.rs`, and from nothing else -- no driver, no `quirin` subcommand, no configured-audit path. This does NOT weaken CT41's stage rows: constraint 23 requires a stage read `executed` only where a named workspace test runs it on the case's own artifact, and that is exactly what the landed runner does; the stage `atomic_publication_check` means `the composed publication judgment ran on this artifact`, which is true. It is also NOT the CT42-CELL-UNROUTED shape, whose defect was a stage meaning `compile_files ran` that nothing could reach. What it does mean is published rather than implied: no `quirin` invocation on a C file reports this refusal today, so CT41's mapping is evidence about an API and its fixture, not about anything a user of this toolchain currently sees -- a weaker position than `legacy_c`, whose analyzer `quirin-audit` really drives. Discharge: route the judgment from a driver entry point (a `quirin`/`quirin-audit` surface that selects a publication profile over a compile task), or record the decision to keep it an API with its ground. Until then do not describe CT41 as a case the toolchain decides end to end.

named_followups.title: A Lean theorem about CT41's own case class now exists; nothing binds the artifact to it
named_followups.why: Re-verification against main CHANGED this finding, and the change is worth the space. Before the merge the honest statement was that the audited `QCore.AtomicPublication` theorems were reached by the ADMITTED control and not by the case. The landed mapping added `non_atomic_completion_has_no_payload_path` (audited in `AuditAtomicPublication.lean`), which proves that a program whose `flagKind` is `.plain` or `.volatile` has NO payload happens-before path -- a theorem about CT41's own case class, not about its control. So the gap is no longer a missing theorem; it is the BINDING. Nothing takes `compiler/tests/fixtures/ct/CT41/case.c`, derives the Lean `Program` it corresponds to, and checks that theorem against it the way `ct01_proof_leg.rs` binds CT01 through the F02 digest relation; the Rust extractor's `VolatileFlagHasNoSynchronization` and the Lean `flagKind = .volatile` are related by REVIEW, which is exactly constraint 28's Lean-model-to-Rust correspondence premise. CT41's `proof` stage therefore correctly reads `unassessed` on main and the proof numerator correctly stays 5. The practical consequence is that a CT41 proof leg is now a realistic next card rather than a research problem -- the theorem is already there and already audited. Discharge: a named host-unconditional test binding this case's artifact to that theorem, with the correspondence it assumes stated, and a deliberate edit to the pinned `PROOF_GATED_CASES` table. Do not read the existing audit as CT41's proof in the meantime.

named_followups.title: CT41 is the first case to supersede the wave-9 control clause rather than satisfy it, and the general rule is undecided
named_followups.why: Two independent mappings of CT41 were built from the same base and reached the same row. Both measured the SAME obstruction -- that the wave-9 attribution rule's clause (b), `a control that removes exactly that construct and moves the verdict`, cannot be met literally for this case -- and that agreement, reached separately, is the substance. They then took different exits. The landed card SUPERSEDES the clause for CT41 only, saying so in `docs/agents/evidence.md`, and substitutes protocol replacement: volatile and plain both refuse, a matching release/acquire control checks, relaxed arms refuse, and removing `volatile` must never confer ordering. The unlanded one read `the construct the scenario names` at the MECHANISM level -- `volatile used as a completion flag` naming a mechanism rather than a token -- and claimed the same controls satisfy the clause as written. The reason a literal reading is unavailable is now a shipped fixture rather than an argument: `volatile_atomic_ops.c` is the one-token edit toward the admitted side and C11 itself refuses it, so no admitted one-token neighbour of `case.c` exists in the language. WHAT IS UNDECIDED is the general rule. The superseding form is per-case and visible; the mechanism-level reading is general and silent, and would let a future card call any multi-site control `removing exactly that construct` with no declaration anywhere. Discharge: decide, in the routed constraint page rather than in a report, whether clause (b) is read at token level with per-case supersessions declared (the landed form) or at construct level generally; if the former, the next case of this shape declares its own supersession and does not inherit CT41's.

named_followups.title: CT41's fixture pins the one-publisher/one-successful-consumer bounds; nothing establishes them
named_followups.why: The route admits exactly `publisher_invocations: 1` and `successful_consumer_invocations: 1`, and card CT41-SYNC-MODEL states in its own words that these are caller-declared premises: the AST proves the static declarations, source order and absence of other visible accesses and entry references, and explicitly does not prove dynamic call counts. The landed fixture records the pair in `expected.json` and the landed runner asserts both on the issued certificate, so the premise is visible in the case record rather than only in the runner -- but pinning a premise is not discharging it. Re-verified against main: the case's own refusal does not depend on them (the landed route checks the full publication shape and access inventory first, then attributes the qualifier refusal, and neither step reads an invocation count), so the exposure is entirely on the ADMITTED control, whose happens-before claim is conditional on a bound nothing checks. Discharge: derive the invocation bounds from a whole-program fact, or state the conditionality in any text that cites the control's certificate. Do not let the certificate be quoted without its bounds.

named_followups.title: The historical typed_source qualifier branch still cannot tell volatile from _Atomic; CT41 no longer needs it to
named_followups.why: This is the half of the retired CT41-TYPED-SOURCE-UNDISCRIMINATING that the mapping does not discharge, carried forward under its own name so retiring the parent does not lose it. Re-verified on the landed tree: `crates/qcore-c-gateway/src/typed_source.rs:522` still refuses `volatile`, `_Atomic` and `restrict` in ONE branch with ONE message (`qualified access requires additional synchronization/alias evidence`) -- fail-closed and correct for that importer, and still unable to express the very distinction CT41 is about. CT41 maps on a different arm entirely, the atomic-publication route, whose flag classification DOES draw the distinction; card CT41-MAP's added `qualified_atomic.c` control is what measures that, refusing a `volatile _Atomic int` as `UnsupportedAtomicFlag` rather than under the volatile arm whose sentence would be false of it. Any later card wanting a qualifier-sensitive answer in the typed-source import path must still supply it there. Discharge: split the branch into per-qualifier arms with their own messages and controls, or record the decision that one wholesale refusal is the right answer for that importer with its ground.

named_followups.title: Nothing in this corpus says what volatile IS for; CT41 says only what it is not
named_followups.why: CT41's mapping establishes that a `volatile` completion flag buys no synchronization proof. The complement -- whether a use of `volatile` for its actual C11 purposes (a memory-mapped device register, an object accessed from a signal handler, an object live across `setjmp`) is expressible, judged or even admitted anywhere in this toolchain -- is measured nowhere, by either CT41 card or any other. The legacy resource projection derives no fact about it; the atomic-publication route refuses every volatile flag by construction, and since the landed change does so only after validating the full publication shape, it says nothing at all about a volatile object that is not a completion flag; the typed_source importer refuses the qualifier wholesale (see CT41-TYPED-SOURCE-QUALIFIER-ARM-STILL-UNDISCRIMINATING). No CT case names it, so no row is missing and nothing is overstated -- this is registered so that `CT41 is mapped` and `50/50` are not read as `volatile is handled`. Discharge: measure the three complement shapes through whatever route would see them and record what each answers, or record that the corpus deliberately asks nothing about them.

named_followups.title: With the CT corpus fully mapped, the unmapped-bucket label machinery is exercised on scratch facts only
named_followups.why: Mapping the last case left `unmapped_labels`, `unmapped_bucket_counts`, `unmapped_label_sources`, the supersession rule and the retirement rule with ZERO live instances on disk: the committed tree's label map is empty. The landed mapping repaired the consequence -- `scripts/tests/test_ct_stage_summary.py` gained an `unmap_ct41()` helper called at eight sites that restores the exemplar in each scratch tree, and one test now asserts `unmapped_labels(ROOT) == {}` directly. Card CT41-MAP reached the same repair independently on its own branch and DROPPED it as duplicate; what it adds is the finding rather than the fix, plus one measurement worth recording: on a tree where the mapping card's retirement was the only one, `test_retiring_a_still_unmapped_case_fails_closed` could pass through the WRONG rule (`two evidence records retire this case`) instead of the live-label rule it names, because the card's own retirement supplied the second. The landed `unmap_ct41()` withdraws that retirement and so reaches the right rule -- verified here by reading `ct_stage_summary._lane_row_retirements`, whose unmapped check precedes its staleness check -- but the hazard is generic: a test that reaches its refusal is not thereby testing its own rule. What does not go away is that there is no candidate left to promote to a tree fact, so the mechanism is verified against scratch trees this test file builds and never against the repository disagreeing with itself; a regression returning an empty map is invisible to the committed-tree arm except through that one direct assertion. Discharge: keep that assertion, add the tally-sum and `ct_unmapped` zero arms beside it, and if a future card ever unmaps a case or adds CT51+, restore a live exemplar and say so; otherwise record the decision that the mechanism is scratch-verified for good.

named_followups.title: Compose the selected Monkey callbacks with Cycle 18 event semantics
named_followups.why: Narrowed by W43-MONKEY-CALLBACK-COMPOSITION; not retired, 0/3 callbacks composed. The seven obligations the bounded aggregate leaves unresolved are now measured per callback and per imported source path by `quirin-audit cycle18-obligations` over the rechecked aggregate and the same pinned compile task: 51 relevant callback/path/obligation cells over 3 callbacks and 8 paths, 5 discharged before (joined native families: cb_event 4/4 controlled executions, cb_wait_2_timeout 1/1) and 17 after. Discharged as source facts: initialization reachability for all three callbacks (_mk_event_init returns the literal 0 on its only imported path under the selected Unix profile, refuting loop-create path 0) and natural activation for cb_timeout and cb_wait_2_timeout (no imported operation reads the activation flags). Each callback keeps an individual Unknown reason. cb_event: caller null handling; caller size bounds; fired-array write authority (ctx->fired[fired_count] has no capacity guard, and its natural-activation entry state reduces to the same bound, path selection being settled by exhaustive single-bit guards); registration (event_new result unchecked in _mk_event_add; 16 of _mk_event_update's 24 paths return -1 after freeing the old event without replacing ev_map->event). cb_timeout: caller null handling; argument-ownership provenance (registration-local exclusivity derived from _mk_event_timeout_create, whole-program accessor non-use not established); registration (event_new, event_add and _mk_event_add results unchecked; release after the non-teardown path needs a later teardown activation before base free); all-path coverage narrowed to the close-failure branch of its ignored evutil_closesocket(ev_map->pipe[1]) - all three paths compose as source-derived Cycle 18 event programs on the close-success branch. cb_wait_2_timeout: caller null handling; registration (event_new and event_add unchecked in _mk_event_wait_2). All three remain blocked by the fault-model provisional-Unsafe scenarios base_creation_failure and fired_allocation_failure, and cb_wait_2_timeout also by timer_creation_failure; these are not validated upstream defects. Earlier bounded evidence (observed timed wait, priority-one failure classification, four-path payload, timeout self-teardown, the 3-family/8-path aggregate) is unchanged. Discharge: per callback, every relevant obligation of every path discharged by source/build/profile-bound composition with no relevant provisional-Unsafe scenario left; this needs a complete production caller inventory for mk_event_loop_create and either a changed Monkey source or a proof that its unchecked creation/registration results cannot fail. named_followups.title: No mechanism stops a delegated card from advancing main; the rule is policy alone
named_followups.why: MAIN-GUARD-REMOVAL (2026-09-23) removed the versioned main-ref guard that CARD-SCOPE-GUARD added in wave 36 after the wave-33 incident, at the integrator's direction: the .githooks reference-transaction and pre-push hooks, their shared decision script, scripts/install_main_guard.py and both guard test files are deleted, and the seven MAIN-GUARD-* entries describing that guard's reach retire with it. docs/agents/operations.md keeps 'a delegated card never advances main' as policy, but nothing now refuses the wave-33 shape - a card running `git -C <main checkout> merge` or pushing main - so the rule rests on agent briefs and integrator review. named_followups.title: Compose cio_chunk_close's filesystem and unsupported-backend paths before its legs can count
named_followups.why: W43-CHUNK-SOURCE-PROFILE attaches pinned-source compositions to cio_chunk_close and cio_chunk_close_stream. Source paths 2 and 3 - the filesystem-backed close, whose nested cleanup keeps unresolved OS custody, and the unsupported-backend close, whose backend custody is opaque - are not composed, so under the path-completeness rule the reached legs discharge nothing for either function and both rows keep all nine legs outstanding.
