named_followups.title: A whole call under a cast or in parentheses keeps the return-position refusal (26 leaves)
named_followups.why: Card W43-RETURN-EXPRESSION lowers a whole-call return whose synthetic assignment the statement classifier refuses to that refusal, but only when the call's name is the expression's first token and its `)` the last. The census (docs/reports/w43-return-expression/census/) measures 25 Unknown-function leaves over 20 functions where the call sits under one or more `( TYPE-NAME )` casts: 23 uncontracted or builtin callees and 2 contracted `Owned{nullable}` callees (`(T *) rd_kafka_mem_calloc(...)`); 11 leaves are sole blockers. One more leaf is a whole call wrapped in redundant parentheses (`return (LZ4F_decodeHeader(...));`), which the Rust rule reads literally and does not strip. The uncontracted half would be a pure re-attribution; the contracted `Owned` half would be an ADMISSION that escapes a fresh site through a cast, which needs its own argument that a pointer or integer conversion preserves (or does not) the escaped identity. Discharge: a card that recognises a leading cast positively (type-name tokens only, never a parenthesised expression or function designator), lowers the refused half as W43 does, and either admits the Owned half with a Lean statement about conversions or refuses it by name, with a measured arbiter.

named_followups.title: Return expressions with a call inside a larger expression stay refused (82 leaves)
named_followups.why: Card W43-RETURN-EXPRESSION measured 82 refused return leaves over 76 Unknown functions whose expression contains a call but is not one whole call: 53 with an uncontracted call in arithmetic or comparison (`strcmp(a, b) == 0`), 18 conditionals and 9 short-circuits over a call, and 2 whose calls are all contracted; 41 leaves (39 functions) are sole blockers. B01 already admits exactly one externally declared contracted `None` call in a scalar residual; everything else needs an evaluation model for a call whose result feeds further computation, and a conditional or short-circuit call is not unconditionally evaluated (constraint 5d). Discharge: a measured card that either lowers the refused-call subset to the classifier's refusal of the call with a proved frequency-preserving decomposition, or states per sub-shape why it stays refused.

named_followups.title: 290 access-only return expressions are refused for their operands' binding and typing, not for the return

named_followups.title: Clauses after `contract inherit PARENT` are refused (QI002); no sound per-consumer extension rule exists yet
named_followups.why: Card CONTRACT-INHERIT refuses `contract inherit P { … };`. Whether an added clause is sound depends on the consumer and the clause family: in resource v1 a `requires resource_literal_argument(p, LITERAL);` premise only withdraws call sites and would be a sound strengthening, while an added `ensures normal resource_*` mode duplicates a parameter's mode, which v1 refuses and for which v1 has no strength order at all. A sound admission rule therefore has to be stated per consumer and per clause family, with a Lean theorem that every admitted extension only strengthens (never weakens) the inherited obligations, and a v1 loader check that the extended child's loaded record differs from the parent's only in the admitted direction. Discharge: specify and prove that rule for resource v1 premises (at least), implement it with negative controls for every non-admitted family, or record a decision that extensions stay refused.

named_followups.title: Only the resource-v1 loader consumes inherited contracts; observation, lifecycle and source-bound interpreters refuse them
named_followups.why: Card CONTRACT-INHERIT's elaboration (elaborate_contract_module) is interpreter-independent and proves (Lean rename_preserves_meaning) that the positional renaming preserves meaning for any reading that resolves clause words by parameter lookup, but a consumer that reads some positions structurally can diverge (Lean positional_reading_can_diverge), so each consumer must compare its own reading of child and parent before trusting an inherited contract. Only the resource-v1 loader has that comparison. contract_observation, chunk_contract, the lifecycle and source-bound adapters and the frontend's contract envelope all receive unresolved inclusion as a Q000 parse refusal (fail-closed), which is correct but means an observation or lifecycle policy cannot be inherited. Discharge: for each consumer that should accept inherited contracts, add its reading-equality gate over elaborated text with negative controls, or record that it stays refusing.

named_followups.title: The two derived-pointer violation candidates (`invalid_release`, `use_after_release`) reach no function of the pinned corpus
named_followups.why: Card W43-LIBC-RESULT-ALIAS added `LegacyDiagnosticKind::InvalidRelease` (an interior pointer from a declared derived result handed to a release) and `UseAfterRelease` (a derived pointer used, released or returned on a path where its base was released), both reported from settled states by `report_derived_pointer_violations`. They are unit-tested in crates/qcore-c-gateway/tests/derived_result.rs and modelled in QCore.DerivedResult, but the arbiter over the 185 pinned units added **zero** leaves of either category: no modeled use or release of a derived binding in the corpus follows a release of a tracked base, and no interior result reaches a release. The unchanged provisional-Unsafe count therefore records the absence of such code in the corpus, not a verification of the arms (the RETURN-POSITION-ACCUSING-UNEXERCISED-IN-CORPUS shape). Discharge condition: a pinned or held-out real-code fixture in which a declared derived result's base is released before a use, or an interior result is released, reaches the arm, with the leaf attributed and never presented as an upstream defect.

named_followups.title: A derived result that dropped `const` records it, but no check refuses a write through it at a borrowed position
named_followups.why: Card W43-LIBC-RESULT-ALIAS's loader sets `const_dropped` on a derived result whose base is `ptr<const, u8>` under a `ptr<mut, u8>` result (`strchr`, `strrchr`, `strstr`, `strcasestr`, `memchr`, `memrchr`), and the gateway carries it on the derived binding through copies, joins and re-derivation (QCore.DerivedResult.const_dropped_survives_derivation). A direct write through such a pointer (`*p = 0`) is already refused by the indirect-store gate, but a contracted callee that writes through a `resource_borrowed` parameter (`memcpy(p, ...)`, `strcpy(p, ...)`) is not distinguished from one that reads, because the v1 vocabulary has no per-parameter read/write fact and the transfer function does not see declared ABI types. Writing through a pointer derived from an object defined `const` is undefined (C11 6.7.3p6), but that is a const-correctness property outside the custody projection. Discharge condition: either a read/write distinction on borrowed parameters (or the declared `ptr<mut, …>` type threaded to the transfer function) with a refusal at a const-dropped actual, measured on the corpus, or a recorded decision that const-correctness stays outside the published verdict's property.

named_followups.title: Returning a derived result is refused, so a wrapper that returns `memcpy(...)` or `strcasestr(...)` stays Unknown
named_followups.why: Card W43-LIBC-RESULT-ALIAS refuses every escape of a derived pointer (`return p;` with `p` derived, and `legacy_return_call::escapes_only_fresh_custody` answers false for `Derived`), because escaping it would either discharge the base (an alias is not fresh custody) or publish a pointer the caller cannot release. W4 has no inferred mode for "the result is derived from parameter k" either. Measured cost at the arbiter: `rdxxhash.c` `XXH_memcpy` (`return memcpy(dest, src, size);`), the eighth memcpy-sole-blocked function LIBC-MEM-RESULT-ALIAS counted, and `mk_string.c` `mk_string_casestr` (`return strcasestr(heystack, needle);`) each exchange their uncontracted-call leaf for a return-expression refusal and stay Unknown. Discharge condition: an inferred (validated) derived-result summary for a body whose every exit returns a pointer derived from one borrowed formal, with Lean parity and a re-arbiter, or a recorded refusal.

named_followups.title: Releasing an exact alias (`free(memcpy(b, ...))`) is refused rather than credited as the base's release
named_followups.why: The card brief asked that releasing any derived result be a violation candidate and not a release of the base. For an EXACT alias that is false of C: `memcpy` returns the value of its first argument, so `free(memcpy(b, s, n))` frees `b` validly. Card W43-LIBC-RESULT-ALIAS therefore splits the rule by extent: an interior pointer handed to a release is an `invalid_release` candidate; an exact alias handed to a release, consumption, store, removal, reallocation or return is refused (`unknown_alias`, the base marked with an unresolved effect so no leak is claimed) and never credited to the base. Crediting it would be faithful but is the discharging direction and needs its own measured admission. No corpus function reaches the shape at the arbiter. Discharge condition: a measured decision to credit an exact alias's release to its base (with Lean parity: the alias's value equals the base's), or this refusal kept on a recorded ground.

named_followups.title: `realpath` (argument 2 or fresh allocation) and `pthread_getspecific` (retained storage) stay undeclared
named_followups.why: Of W43-LIBC-RESULT-ALIAS-NAMES's list, card W43-LIBC-RESULT-ALIAS declared the exact aliases (`memcpy`, `memmove`, `memset`, `strcpy`, `strncpy`, `gmtime_r`, `localtime_r`) and the interior pointers (`strchr`, `strrchr`, `strstr`, `strcasestr`, `memchr`, `memrchr`) and refused two by name. `realpath(path, resolved)` returns `resolved` when it is non-null and otherwise a fresh `malloc` allocation the caller must free: its result mode depends on an argument's value, which v1 cannot state (C04.4, no value-dependent modes; `resource_literal_argument(resolved, 0)` could restrict a declaration to the fresh arm, but function names are unique across a selection, so the derived arm would stay undeclared). `pthread_getspecific(key)` returns a pointer an earlier `pthread_setspecific` retained, which aliases no argument of this call. Measured at the baseline: 1 leaf / 1 function for `realpath`, 16 leaves / 15 functions for `pthread_getspecific`; `realpath` sole-blocks no function and `pthread_getspecific` one. Discharge condition: a value-conditional result reading of `realpath` (owned when `resolved` is NULL, derived otherwise) with Lean parity, measured on the corpus, or its literal-premise fresh arm alone; and a retained-storage mode (or recorded refusal) for `pthread_getspecific` together with W43-LIBC-CALLBACK-RETAIN's `pthread_setspecific`.

named_followups.why: Card W43-LIBC-RESULT-ALIAS repaired the declared-ABI reader (W43-LIBC-POINTER-QUALIFIER-READER) and measured the fourteen prototypes card W43-LIBC-CONTRACTS withdrew, through the same census tool over the 185 captured units (docs/reports/w43-libc-result-alias/abi-evidence.json): printf, fprintf, snprintf and sprintf now agree in all 168 units that declare them; stat (109), strftime (144), gettimeofday (107), getsockopt (105), dlsym (4), cnd_timedwait (83), pthread_sigmask (5) and regerror (1) agree everywhere they are declared; getpeername agrees in 12 units and is still withdrawn in 93, where `_GNU_SOURCE` spells its address as the `__SOCKADDR_ARG` transparent union (W43-LIBC-ABI-READER-SHAPES' bind/connect shape); regexec is still withdrawn in its 1 unit because `regmatch_t __pmatch[__restrict_arr]` puts the qualifier inside an array bound, which the reader refuses. named_followups.title: flb_strdup/flb_strndup contracts are trusted assumptions over static inline header bodies the analyzer could read, and the pinned corpus has no call site that exercises them
named_followups.why: Card CONTRACT-INHERIT-ADOPTION declared, at the user's direction, fluent_bit/resource_string.qcore: flb_strdup and flb_strndup inherit libc::strdup and libc::strndup, and the module is selected in cycle19-resource-contracts.json. Both are static inline in include/fluent-bit/flb_str.h, so wherever the module is selected the contract stands in for a body the unit carries. flb_strndup is not a byte-exact forward of strndup (memcpy of exactly n bytes through flb_malloc); only the custody statement is the same. The declared-ABI gate agrees in that unit. The assumption therefore has no measured effect yet and no measured evidence either. Discharge: when the corpus scope reaches units that call flb_strdup/flb_strndup, attribute the arbiter delta leaf by leaf and decide, with W4 summaries of the header bodies as the comparison, whether to keep the contract selected or let the analyzer check the bodies (the W43-LIBC-HEADER-INLINE-BODIES precedent for glibc inline bodies).

named_followups.title: A child whose same-typed parameters carry the parent's names in another order is admitted, and binds by position
named_followups.why: Card CONTRACT-INHERIT-QCORE-PROVIDER-NAMING tested inheritance from derived-result parents (CONTRACT-INHERIT-ALIAS-RESULT-PARENTS). A child that reorders its parameters so that a type moves is refused (QI010), but when the moved parameters have one type the reordering is invisible to the signature check: `extern fn app_search(needle: ptr<const, u8>, haystack: ptr<const, u8>) -> ptr<mut, u8> contract inherit libc::strstr;` is admitted, and its elaborated clause is `resource_return_interior(needle, nullable)` with base index 0, exactly the parent's record (compiler/tests/contract_inherit_qcore_provider.rs, swapped_parameter_names_do_not_move_the_base). That is the positional rule C15 states, and it is sound for the declaration as written; but a C wrapper that really swaps its arguments before calling strstr would receive a wrong trusted assumption, and a reader could take the child's parameter names as re-binding the base. The rename check refuses only capture (a child name equal to a non-parameter word), not a child name equal to a parent parameter at a different position. None of the 13 inheriting declarations on the tree has such a name (flb_*, rd_* and mk_* keep the parent's order; rd_strdup/rd_strndup rename s/n to str/len). Discharge: either refuse a child parameter named like a parent parameter at another position (a C15 change with a code, a negative control, a Lean statement over rename_clauses, and a census of the inheriting declarations), or record that the positional rule alone is the intended contract and close this entry with that decision.

named_followups.title: chunkio/memory_close.qcore supports the resource-v1 cio_chunk_close view only on memory-backed chunks
named_followups.why: Card CONTRACT-VIEW-PROJECTION-CHECK checks every multi-module declaration as a registered relation (qcore_contract::contract_views). The relation memory_close.qcore -> resource_open_close.qcore holds only under the computed, pinned premise nonnull_chunk_has_memory_backend, classified Coverage: outside it the detailed contract says nothing about the chunk (Lean QCore.ContractViewProjection.outside_the_memory_backend_the_view_is_not_implied), while chunkio/resource_open_close.qcore's resource_released(chunk, nonnull) is applied by the resource loader to every call whatever the backend. The filesystem and unsupported-backend policies (filesystem_chunk_close.qcore, unsupported_close.qcore) declare other names and are not related to the view. Nothing moves a verdict: the view was already a trusted assumption. Discharge: a checked relation from a source-checked declaration of cio_chunk_close covering the other backends to the view, or a premise on the view that narrows it to what is supported.

named_followups.title: The resource-v1 views are entailed only under detailed premises the v1 checker does not enforce
named_followups.why: Card CONTRACT-VIEW-PROJECTION-CHECK computes, for each projection, which detailed requires clauses the view's own custody discipline discharges; the rest are pinned per relation with a class (Profile, Environment, Coverage). flb_malloc/flb_calloc/flb_free assume ordinary_allocator_profile == 1 (Profile, fixed for the audited build). chunk_destructor.qcore -> resource_open_close.qcore assumes chunk_is_not_busy and chunk_has_no_task_or_route_custody (Environment). memory_close.qcore -> resource_open_close.qcore assumes nine premises besides its Coverage one (seven Environment: disjoint owned provenance, live reciprocal and distinct link memberships, context/stream lifetime, counter coverage, no lock/busy/task/route/transaction obligations, exclusive access; two Profile: cross-unit source/ABI bindings, free resolving to libc). The v1 vocabulary has no clause for any of them, so every call site the view covers assumes them. named_followups.title: The view-entailment decision procedure's exactness is argued, not proved in Lean

Its exactness rests on a small-model argument documented in the Rust module; the Lean model (QCore.ContractViewProjection) proves each registered entailment directly over the integers and that dropping premises is sound, but not the enumeration lemma itself, and the fragment evaluator's parity with the shared interpreter is a Rust test over a grid. Discharge: a Lean proof of the small-model lemma for the fragment, or an extraction of the Rust enumerator.

named_followups.title: An access inside a call's arguments or result assignment stays refused: 9,539 leaves on 2,408 Unknown functions, 242 sole-blocked
named_followups.why: Card W43-INDIRECT-ACCESS-GENERAL admits only statements with no call (the typed scalar-access route is never consulted for a statement that carries one). Measured at its AFTER census (docs/reports/w43-indirect-access-general/residuals.txt, class call-argument): 9,539 leaves of the five access-refusal families in 2,408 Unknown functions, 242 of them blocked by that family alone. These are `f(p->x)`, `x = f(p->x)` and `p->f = g()`; the borrowed-actual, bound-read and member-address routes already admit narrow cases. Admitting one needs the call's own contract (and, for an uncontracted callee, the call leaf remains: the census-2 exchange proxy). DISCHARGE: a card that admits a typed scalar access in a Borrowed data argument or as a call result's scalar destination, with the call's existing obligations retained, and a measured re-pin; or a recorded decision that the class belongs to the call routes.

named_followups.title: Member chains of depth two or more stay refused: 5,616 leaves on 2,057 Unknown functions, 188 sole-blocked
named_followups.why: The typed scalar-access route admits one selection per access (`*B`, `B[I]`, `B->F`, `S.F`). `a->b->c`, `a->b.c` and `a[i].f` stay refused. Measured at the AFTER census (residuals.txt, class chain): 5,616 leaves (3,998 indirect-access, 1,306 unsupported-assignment, 199 increment, 113 unrecognized-destination) in 2,057 Unknown functions, 188 sole-blocked. The intermediate member is a pointer loaded from memory, which the projection binds only through a field link; admitting it needs the intermediate dereference's own obligation (the owner's field link live, or the owner untracked) and a member reader that classifies the intermediate (census-2 section 7 measured most chains end Unresolved). DISCHARGE: a card that extends the route to record-pointer member chains with each intermediate dereference checked against field links, Lean parity and a measured re-pin; or a measured decision that the reader classes do not justify it.

named_followups.title: Single accesses whose base or member the declaration reader does not classify stay refused: 3,136 leaves on 1,212 Unknown functions, 94 sole-blocked
named_followups.why: A single `*B`, `B[I]`, `B->F` or `S.F` is admitted only when the reader commits to `SCALAR *B`/`SCALAR B[N]`, `struct T *B` with a scalar member `F` of a completely read `struct T`, or `struct T S`. Measured at the AFTER census (residuals.txt, class untyped-single-access): 3,136 leaves (2,668 indirect-access, 247 unrecognized-destination, 187 store-through, 19 unsupported-assignment, 15 increment) in 1,212 Unknown functions, 94 sole-blocked. The causes are the readers already registered (RECORD-BODY-TOTAL-OR-REJECT, TYPEDEF-ANONYMOUS-AGGREGATE-UNREACHED, BASE-CAUSE-SECOND-DISCOUNT-PARTIAL) plus pointees the rule deliberately excludes (`void *`, `T **`, records). A reader repair now has a consumer: every base it commits to reaches this route. DISCHARGE: re-measure this class after any of those reader repairs lands, and attribute the moves to the reader, not the route; or a recorded decision that the class is closed.

named_followups.title: Pointer-valued stores through a single access stay refused: 306 leaves on 207 Unknown functions, 18 sole-blocked
named_followups.why: `p->f = q`, `*pp = q` and `a[i] = q` store an identity, which is an escape or custody question. The existing member-link (aggregate store) and out-slot machinery state that effect only for their own premises; card W43-INDIRECT-ACCESS-GENERAL admits no pointer-valued store. Measured at the AFTER census (residuals.txt, class pointer-value-store): 306 leaves (249 indirect-access, 43 store-through, 10 unrecognized-destination, 4 unsupported-assignment) in 207 Unknown functions, 18 sole-blocked. DISCHARGE: a card that states the custody effect of storing a tracked or untracked pointer into an untracked object (publication? escape? loss of the residual claim?) and admits exactly that, with Lean parity and a measured re-pin.

named_followups.title: Stores through a moving or computed pointer stay refused: 335 leaves on 172 Unknown functions
named_followups.why: `*p++ = c` increments the pointer it dereferences (C11 6.5.2.4), and `*(p + i) = c` dereferences a computed pointer; neither is a typed scalar access, so card W43-INDIRECT-ACCESS-GENERAL refuses both. A tracked pointer that moves becomes an interior pointer to its allocation, which the projection would have to rebind as derived (the W43-LIBC-RESULT-ALIAS vocabulary) before its release could be judged. Measured at the AFTER census (residuals.txt, class pointer-increment): 335 leaves (136 unrecognized-destination, 101 indirect-access, 98 increment) in 172 Unknown functions, 0 sole-blocked. DISCHARGE: a card that models pointer arithmetic on a bound name as an interior derivation of the same site, with the release rules of QCore.DerivedResult, and a measured re-pin.

named_followups.title: Access refusals outside every named shape: 1,693 leaves on 764 Unknown functions, 25 sole-blocked, including uncensused for-clauses
named_followups.why: The residual class `other` of card W43-INDIRECT-ACCESS-GENERAL's AFTER census (residuals.txt): 1,693 leaves (751 indirect-access, 360 increment, 316 unsupported-assignment, 266 unrecognized-destination) in 764 Unknown functions, 25 sole-blocked. It holds expression statements, declarations with bracketed or dotted initializers, compound assignments into names from non-access values, and the increment-family leaves of `for` clauses, which the card's statement census does not stream (it records only `parse_statement`'s statements; 189 such leaves at the BEFORE census). DISCHARGE: stream the for-clause and synthetic-condition statements into the statement census and split this class by shape before any card is cut on it; not a discharge: citing the leaf count.

named_followups.title: The typed scalar access's use_after_release arm reaches no function of the pinned corpus
named_followups.why: Card W43-INDIRECT-ACCESS-GENERAL reports a `use_after_release` candidate when a typed scalar access dereferences a base settled on one identity whose status carries the released bit (`report_indirect_scalar_violations`, from the settled states). It is unit-tested (crates/qcore-c-gateway/tests/indirect_scalar_access.rs: store, read, member and derived cases) and modelled (QCore.IndirectScalarAccess.an_accusation_names_a_released_settled_identity), but the arbiter over the 185 pinned units added zero use_after_release and zero invalid_release leaves: no admitted access in the corpus follows a release of its base. The unchanged provisional-Unsafe count records that absence, not the arm's verification (the RETURN-POSITION-ACCUSING-UNEXERCISED-IN-CORPUS shape). DISCHARGE: a pinned or held-out real-code fixture reaches the arm, with the leaf attributed and never presented as an upstream defect.

named_followups.title: A character-typed store through a pointer may rewrite a tracked pointer object's representation; the frame and the no-undefined-behaviour reading carry the claim
named_followups.why: C lets a character lvalue modify any object's representation (C11 6.5p7), so `*c = 0` or `c[i] = 0` through an untracked `char *c` could rewrite the bytes of a pointer the projection tracks. Card W43-INDIRECT-ACCESS-GENERAL bounds that exactly as the refusal it replaces did: a write through `*B`/`B[I]` poisons every binding outside the constraint-10a frame (a name whose slot no other lvalue designates is spared), and QCore.IndirectScalarAccess states the frame as a premise, not a proof. Two things remain premises: (1) a field link (an aggregate member's tracked child) is not invalidated by such a store, exactly as it is not invalidated by a `memset`/`memcpy` through a Borrowed position today (W43-LIBC-RESULT-ALIAS); (2) a subsequent use of a rewritten pointer is excluded by the no-undefined-behaviour reading. DISCHARGE: invalidate the field links of the targeted site (and of every site, for an untracked base) on a character-typed write, with a measured re-pin; or record that the premise is the same one the Borrowed `memset`/`memcpy` declarations already rest on, in constraint 10a's words.

named_followups.title: A direct write through a const-dropped derived pointer is now admitted, so W43-LIBC-RESULT-ALIAS's 'already refused' sentence no longer holds
named_followups.why: W43-LIBC-RESULT-ALIAS section 1.3 wrote that a direct write through a `const_dropped` derived pointer (a `strchr` result over a `const char *` parameter) is already refused by the indirect-store gate, and registered only the borrowed-position case as W43-RESULT-ALIAS-CONST-WRITE. Card W43-INDIRECT-ACCESS-GENERAL admits `*p = '\0'` through such a pointer when its base resolves, because the flag is set from the contract's parameter type and says nothing about whether the object is const, and constness is outside the custody property (as bounds are; spec L18 and the report's scope field). The forecast mirror counts 1 store and 5 reads through a name the body assigns a derived result in the pinned corpus. DISCHARGE: carry the argument's declared constness (not the parameter's) into the derived binding and refuse a write through a genuinely const object, with a measured re-pin; or fold this into W43-RESULT-ALIAS-CONST-WRITE with a recorded decision that constness stays outside the property.

named_followups.title: The older formal-mutation refusal blocks 15 leaves of typed scalar statements before the new route is consulted
named_followups.why: `classify_simple` refuses `unmodeled expression may mutate a formal resource identity` for any statement with an increment or nested write that mentions a protected name, and `*n` anywhere in a body protects the formal `n`, so `(*n)++` and `p->count++` on a protected `p` never reach card W43-INDIRECT-ACCESS-GENERAL's route (pinned by an_increment_of_a_protected_name_keeps_its_refusal). Measured at the AFTER census (scripts/formal_mutation.py): 118 leaves of that family in Unknown functions, 15 of them (9 functions) statements the typed rule would otherwise admit. The refusal protects a formal's identity from `p++`; an increment of the pointee does not change it. DISCHARGE: narrow the formal-mutation gate to writes of the protected name itself (not of an object it designates), with a test that `p++` on a protected formal still refuses, and a measured re-pin.

named_followups.title: The census-2 proxy's EXCH arm has still met no admission that covers every statement of its shape
named_followups.why: Narrowed from INDIRECT-EXCHANGE-PROXY-UNVALIDATED by card W43-INDIRECT-ACCESS-GENERAL, which published the proxy's per-shape prediction beside its measured outcome for the 17 census-2 shapes its typed rule touches (proxy-validation.txt): of 11 functions the proxy calls CLEAR, 4 measured cleared and 7 kept a leaf only because another statement of the same shape is outside the typed rule; no CLEAR prediction was wrong where the rule covered the shape. The 4 EXCH predictions all kept a leaf for the same reason, so the exchange arm is still unmeasured. DISCHARGE: an admission whose rule covers every statement of a census-2 shape measures that shape's EXCH functions, and the difference is recorded.

named_followups.title: The indirect census omits a destination-refused statement's value-side chains, so a forecast from it misses two-base member copies
named_followups.why: `indirect_census::record` reads only the destination window for an AssignmentDestination refusal, so `a->f = b->g` carries no chain (and no member class) for `b`. Card W43-INDIRECT-ACCESS-GENERAL's forecast mirror therefore refused 98 leaves the implementation admitted (unforecast.txt: all indirect-access, all two-base scalar member copies such as `metric_dst->x = metric_src->x`), which is the whole of its leaf-level forecast miss and its one function-level miss (`cmt_time_from_ns`, whose unit `cmt_time.c` then moved to Safe). The card's statement stream carries whole-statement chains; the indirect stream does not. DISCHARGE: record the whole statement's chains in the indirect census as well, keeping the gate's own window as a separate field, and re-run the forecast.
